docs.title: 文獻​研究​ R5：​怎麼​從​ 8 ​份​伴奏​裡​挑出​最好​的​一份
docs.text:
​這份​研究​要​支援​的​決定​： ​調參數​之前​，​先​重新​設計​原型​ 02 ​的​挑選​分數​（steps/metrics.py）。

​評量​理念​（​使用者​提出​，​當作​需求​，​不需​研究​）： 1. ​忠​於​和弦​表​的​和​聲​結構​。 2. ​不要​大量​照抄​柱式​和弦​提示​。​可以​回收​一部分​，​但​大多​數聽​起來​不該​跟​提示​一樣​。 3. ​不違​反和聲​規則​。 4. ​在​限制​內越​有​變化​越​好​。 5. ​保留​「​不抄​旋律​」​這一項​。

docs.title: 摘要
docs.text:
​建議​：​改成​「​先過​門檻​，​再​排名​」​的​兩階段​挑選​。 ​和​聲忠​實度​改為​門檻​，​不再​是​越​高越​好​。​新增​「​照抄​提示​」​一項​。「​變化​」​改為​「​接近​真人​伴奏​的​範圍​」，​不再​是​越多越好​。​最後用​名次​加總​排名​，​取代​ z ​分數加​總​。

​這個​建議​根據​三個​發現​：

  1. ​現在​的​分數會​獎勵​照抄​柱式​和弦​，​這是​指標​本身​的​問題​。 CTnCTR ​這類​和弦音​比例​，​在​柱式​和弦​上​就是​滿分​。Yeh ​等​人​的​原始​研究​裡​，​最機械​的​「​模板​配和聲​」​在​ CTnCTR ​和​ PCS ​上​都​比​真人​作品​高​（0.91、1.97 ​對​ 0.74、1.42）[1]。D3PIA ​的​聽覺​測試​也​顯示​，​和弦​正確​率​較​高​的​系統​，​聽起​來​的​和​聲​反而​比較​差​ [3]。​所以​忠實度​只能​當​「​及格​線​」，​過了​就​不再​加​分​。
  2. 「​照抄​提示​」​有​現成​的​公式​可以​借用​。 ​沒有​論文​專門量​「​伴奏​和​條件​提示​有​多​像​」（​見​第​ 2 ​節​）。​但​ Whole-Song ​生成​論文有​一個​「​抄襲​程度​」​公式​：​同音​級​、​同​起音​的​音數​ ×2 ÷ ​兩邊​音數​和​ [7]。​把​它​用​在​「​候選​伴奏​ vs ​柱式​和弦​提示​」​上​，​就是​我們​要​的​指標​。​另外​可以​搭配​ mir_eval ​的​音符​比​對​（​起音​ ±50 ms，​並比​對長​度​），​抓​出​「​連長​度​都​一樣​」​的​照抄​ [8]。
  3. 「​變化​越多越好​」​沒有​證據​支持​，「​接近​真人​的​範圍​」​才​有​。 ​真人​音樂​的​音級​熵​比​模型​生成​的​低​，​小節間​節奏​一致性​也​比​較​高​ [5]。​直接​最大化​某個​品質​分數​，​會​讓​輸出​失去​多樣​性​、​跑​出怪​東西​ [23]。​所以​變化​要​用​「​離​真人​參考​範圍​多近​」​來評​。

​最大​的​保留​： ​找​不到​任何​研究​證明​這些​符號​指標​和​人耳評​分逐​首相​關​ [4][5]；​綜述​也​認為​生成​音樂​還沒有​通用​的​評量​方法​ [25]。​指標​只能​幫​你​初選​，​最​後​仍​要​靠​你​的​耳朵​。​建議​下​一輪順​便​做​一個​小驗證​：​你​盲​聽​「​指標​選​的​」​和​「​隨機​一份​」，​看​指標​是否​真的​有​幫助​。

docs.title: 1. ​和​聲忠​實度​：​怎麼量​「​有​沒​有​守住​和弦​表​」
docs.text:
• CTnCTR、PCS、MCTD（Yeh ​等​人​，JNMR 2021）。 ​公式​已​從​論文​原文​確認​ [1]：
  • CTnCTR =（​和弦音​＋​合理​的​非​和弦音​）÷（​和弦音​＋​全部​非​和弦音​）。「​合理​」​指距​離下​一個音​兩個​半音​以內​。
  • PCS：​每個​音​和​和弦音​之間​，​同​度​、​三度​、​五度​、​六度​記​ +1，​四度​記​ 0，​其他​記​ −1，​每​十六分音​符​平均​一次​。
  • MCTD：​在​ 6 ​維調性​空間裡​，​旋律​音​和​和弦​之間​的​平均​距離​。

​重點​： ​這三個​指標​原本​是​用​來評​「​旋律​ vs ​和弦​」，​不是​評​伴奏​。​作者​也​提醒​只能​拿來​看​趨勢​，​不能​拿來​判斷​好​壞​ [1]。​我們​目前​把​ CTnCTR ​套​在​伴奏​上​，​柱式​和弦​自然​拿​滿分​。 - ​和弦​正確​率​（Chord Accuracy）。 ​用​自動​和弦​辨識​辨認​生成​的​伴奏​，​逐拍​和​條件​和弦​比​對​根音​加​和弦​性質​，​算​吻合​比例​ [2]。D3PIA ​另外​用​和弦​嵌入​的​餘​弦​相似​度​（Chord Similarity）​給​部分​分數​ [3]。FIGARO ​則用​多標​籤​ F1 [6]。 - ​和弦​正確​率​高​，​不​代表​好​聽​。 ​在​ D3PIA ​的​ 13 ​人​聽覺​測試​中​，WSG ​的​和弦​正確​率​（87.6%）​比​ D3PIA（80.1%）​高​，​和​聲​評分​卻​比​較​低​。​作者​把​原因​歸​於​ WSG ​有​ 2.4% ​的​調外音​ [3]。​這個​測試​人​數少​，​也​沒​有​算​相關​係​數​（​信心​：​中​）。 - ​低音​。 ​沒​找到​評​「​低音​／​根音​有​沒​有​落​在​和弦​換的​地方​」​的​已​發表​指標​。​和弦​辨識​只​比​對​和弦​名稱​的​根音​，​不看​實際​發出​的​最低音​ [2]。 - ​稀疏​的​陷阱​。 ​和弦音​比例​的​分母​是​音數​，​所以​只彈​幾個​長​音​的​伴奏​也​會​拿​高分​。​這是​研究​助理​的​推論​，​文獻​沒有​直接​說​；​它​跟​原型​ 02 ​第一版​挑​到​「​只有​ 4 ​個音​」​的​伴奏​的​情況​一致​。

docs.title: 2. ​照抄​提示​：​怎麼量​「​跟​柱式​和弦​提示​有​多​像​」
docs.text:
• ​沒有​現成​的​「​和​條件​提示​相似​度​」​指標​。 ​文獻中​的​抄襲​指標​都​是​拿​生成​結果​和​訓練​資料​比​ [11][12]。
  • ​最​直接​可用​的​公式​：Whole-Song ​的​「​抄襲​程度​」（Degree of Copying）[7]：
  • sim = 2 ×（​兩邊​同音​級​、​同​起音​的​音數​）÷（​候選​音數​＋​提示音​數​），​範圍​ 0 ​到​ 1。
  • ​原論​文用​來​檢查​有​沒​有​背下​訓練​資料​，​拿來​比​「​候選​ vs ​提示​」​是​我們​的​延伸​用法​。
  • mir_eval ​的​音符​比​對​ [8]：
  • ​預設​是​起音​ ±50 ms、​音高​ ±50 cent，​音​的​結束​時間​必須​落​在​參考長​度​的​ 20%（​至少​ 50 ms）​以內​。​配對​方式​是​二分​圖​最大​配對​。
  • ​可以​分成​「​只​看​起音​」​和​「​連長​度​也​一樣​」​兩種​。​後​者​最能​抓​到​「​原封​不動​照彈​柱式​和弦​」。
  • ​節奏​格子​相似​度​（Grooving Similarity）。 ​把​每小節​分成​ 64 ​格​，​標出​有​起音​的​格子​，​再​比​對​兩份​ [5]。​原版​用​ XOR，​兩邊​都​沒彈​的​格子​也​算​「​相同​」，​所以​稀疏​的​伴奏​會​被​判成​很​像​提示​。FIGARO ​和​一篇​ 2026 ​年​的​鋼琴​編曲​論文​改用​餘弦​相似​度​，​可以​避開​這個​問題​ [6][13]。
  • SSIMuse ​把​影像​的​結構​相似​度​（SSIM）​用​在​鋼琴​捲​簾​上​，​能​同時​比​對​音高​和​長​度​ [12]（​預​印本​，​信心​：​中​）。
  • Yin ​等​人​的​原​創性​報告​（SN Computer Science 2022）​以​「​人類​作曲家​互相​借用​的​程度​」​為​基準​來​判斷​抄太多​ [11]。​本輪​沒​拿到​全文​，​公式​未​確認​（​信心​：​低​）。
  • ​節奏​相似​度​和​人​耳​感受​不​一定​一致​。 ​一篇​鼓組​研究​發現​，XOR ​或漢明​距離​和​人​感受​到​的​相似​程度​相關性​較​弱​ [27]（​學位​論文​，​信心​：​低到​中​）。

docs.title: 3. ​規則​與​可​演奏​性
docs.text:
• music21 ​的​聲部​進行​檢查​ [14]：
  • VoiceLeadingQuartet ​可以​檢查​平行​五度​、​八度​、​同​度​、​隱伏​五​八度​、​聲部​交錯​和​聲部​重疊​。
  • ​它​要​的​是​單音​線條​，​所以​鋼琴​伴奏​得​先​拆出​聲部​才能​用​。
  • ​它​沒​有​導音​解決​、​七音​解決​和​聲部間​距​的​檢查​。
  • ​拆聲部​。 McLeod & Steedman ​的​ HMM ​聲​部分​離有​程式​碼​，​在​巴赫​作品​上測​試過​ [17]。​最​簡單​的​做法​是​「​每個​起音​取​最低音​當​低音​聲部​」，​和​旋律​配成​一對​外聲部​再​檢查​。​這個​做法​本輪​沒​找到​驗證​，​是​未​證實​的​推論​。
  • ​違規次​數要​跟​風格​的​正常值​比​。
  • 「Bach or Mock?」​把​平行​五​八度​等​錯誤​換算成​「​每個​音​的​錯​誤數​ ÷ ​巴赫​本人​的​比例​」[15]。​它用​ 6 ​種特徵​的​分布​距離​評分​，​挑出​真​巴赫​的​正​確率​是​ 92.6%，​專家​只有​ 86.7%。​不過​專家​只有​ 5 ​位​，​而且​這是​辨​真偽​，​不是​和​聽感​評分​的​相關​（​信心​：​中​）。
  • Coconet ​的​訓練​資料​本身​也​有​很多​平行​五​八度​ [16]（​只讀​到​搜尋​摘要​）。​所以​平行​五​八度​不應​該​一出​現​就​淘汰​，​而是​看​比例​。
  • ​協和度​模型​。 Harrison & Pearce（Psychological Review 2020）​的​ incon ​套件​有​ 17 ​種協和度​模型​，​可以​直接​吃​符號​和弦​ [18]。​它​是​ R ​套件​，​用​在​本​專案​得​另外​處理​。​刺耳​音程​重疊​（​我們​已經​有​）​是​更​簡單​的​替代​。
  • ​張力​。 Herremans & Chew ​的​張力​帶​（Tension Ribbons）​在​螺旋​陣列​上算​三種​張力​ [19]。​定義只​部分​確認​（​信心​：​中​）。
  • ​可​演奏​性​：​沒有​經過​同儕​審查​的​自動​指標​。
  • ​鋼琴​難度​模型​有​ RubricNet（​每​隻​手​的​音高​熵​、​音域​、​跳躍率​）[20]，​以及​指法​模型​（PIG ​資料​集​）[21]。RubricNet ​沒有​「​手​的​跨度​」「​同時​幾個音​」​這類​規則​，​也​沒​找到​任何​以​這類​規則評​生成​伴奏​的​研究​。
  • 「​一​隻​手​跨度​不超過​約​ 14 ​個​半音​、​同時​不​超過​ 5 ​個音​」​是​常識​性門檻​，​沒有​文獻​依據​。

docs.title: 4. ​變化​與​創意​，​以及​怎麼​合成​一個​分數
docs.text:
• ​常用​的​變化​指標​ [5][9][10]：
  • ​音級​熵​：12 ​個​音級​的​分布​有​多​平均​。
  • ​小節間​節奏​一致性​（Grooving Similarity，GS）。
  • ​和弦​進行​不​規則度​（CPI）。
  • ​結構​性​（SI）。
  • ​複​音數​（​同時​幾個音​）。
  • ​空拍​比例​。
  • ​音長​分布​、​起音​間​隔​（IOI）。

​有​現成​程式​碼​：MusDr、MusPy、mgeval。 - ​真人​音樂​不​在​極端值​。 ​在​ Wu & Yang ​的​資料裡​，​真人​爵士​的​音級​熵​比​模型​低​（1 ​小節​ 1.94，​模型​ 2.17–2.45），​節奏​一致性​比​模型​高​（0.86，​模型​ 0.69–0.76）[5]。Yang & Lerch ​的​做法​是​比​較​「​和​參考​資料​的​分布​有​多​接近​」，​不是​把​某個​特徵​越拉越​高​ [9]。 - ​只​最大化​一個​分數會​出事​。 SMART ​用​一個​美感​分數​當獎勵​去​強化​鋼琴​生成​，​過度​優化後多樣​性​大幅​下降​，​還出​現重​複​樣式​。​這個​分數​最​後​甚至​把​生成​的​音樂​評得​比​真人​錄音​還高​ [23]。 - ​合成​方式​： - YuE2 ​從​ 8 ​份裡​挑​一份​的​做法​：​先​刪掉​被​其他​候選​全面​勝過​的​（Pareto），​再​依序​只留​「​和​最好​的​差​ 0.10 ​以內​」​的​，​最後挑​剩下​最好​的​一份​ [24]（​只讀​到​搜尋​摘要​，​信心​：​低到​中​）。 - ​有​比賽​用​「​各指標​名次​加總​」（Borda）[28]，​好處​是​不必​把​不同​單位​的​分數​硬​放在​同一​個尺​上​。 - ​沒​找到​比較​這幾種​方法​優劣​的​研究​。 - ​和​人​耳​的​相關性​：​沒有​逐首​的​證據​。 - Jazz Transformer ​的​ 59 ​人​聽覺​測試​沒有算​指標​和​評分​的​相關​ [5]。 - 2025 ​年​的​綜述​沒有​列出​符號​指標​的​人​耳​相關​數字​ [4]；​另​一篇​綜述​認為​沒有​通用​的​評量​方法​ [25]。 - AccoMontage ​的​評量​只有​聽覺​測試​，​沒有​客觀​指標​ [26]。 - ​唯一​的​正面​證據​來​自​一篇​工作坊​論文​：​只有​ 5 ​位評​分者​，​而且​是​模型​層級​的​排名​，​不是​逐首​ [22]。

docs.title: 跨​面向​的​發現
docs.text:
• ​忠實度​和​不​照抄​互相​拉扯​。 「​完美​守住​和弦​表​」​最​便宜​的​做法​，​就是​照彈​柱式​和弦​。​只要​忠實度​是​越​高越​好​，​挑選​就​會​一直​偏向​照抄​。​所以​忠實度​必須​是​門檻​（​及格​就​好​），​照抄​度​另外​扣分​。​這是​現在​挑選​方式​的​根本​問題​。
  • ​三個​面向​都​有​「​稀疏​陷阱​」。 ​和弦音​比例​、​節奏​格子​相似​度​（XOR ​版​）、​刺耳​重疊​，​都​會​讓​「​彈得​很少​」​的​候選​佔​便宜​。​所以​「​至少​要彈​多少​」​得​是​硬門檻​：​音數​、​空拍​比例​。
  • 「​創意​」​在​文獻裡​等​於​「​接近​真人​範圍​內​的​變化​」。 ​不能​用​「​變化​越多越好​」​來​實現​使用者​的​第​ 4 ​條​理念​。​合理​的​做法​是​先​限制​在​真人​伴奏​的​範圍​內​，​再​在​範圍​內​鼓勵​小節​之間​有​變化​。

docs.title: 建議​的​挑選​設計​（​給​ metrics.py）
docs.text:
​以下​是​根據​上面​文獻​組合​出來​的​設計​，​沒有​任何​一篇​論文​完整​驗證過​，​信心​以​各條​引用​為準​。

​第一​階段​：​門檻​。 ​沒過​的​候選​不​排名​；​全部​都​沒過​時​，​才​退回​原本​的​作法​。

​門檻​ ​指標​ ​起始值​（​可調​） ​依據​ ​彈得夠​多​ ​音數​ ≥ ​小節數​，​空拍​比例​ ≤ 25% ​沿用​＋​新增​ [10]、​稀疏​陷阱​ ​不抄​旋律​ ​抄​旋律​比例​ < 0.5 ​沿用​ ​原型​ 02 ​不​照抄​提示​ ​抄襲​程度​（​同音​級​＋​同​起音​）< 0.5 ​新增​，​對應​「​大多​數​不要​一樣​」 [7] ​守住​和弦​ ​逐拍​和弦​吻合​率​ ≥ 0.7，​調外音​ ≤ 5%（​門檻​值​無文獻​依據​） ​改為​門檻​ ​指標​ [2][3]；「​當門檻​」​的​理由​ [1][3] ​彈​得到​ ​同時​發聲​的​伴奏​音​ ≤ 5 ​個​，​且​跨度​ ≤ 14 ​個​半音​（​約​一個​十度​） ​新增​，​無文獻​依據​ ​常識​

​第二​階段​：​在​通過​的​候選裡​排名​。 ​每項​先算​名次​（1 ​到​ N），​名次​加總​最小​的​勝出​ [28]。​不用​ z ​分數加​總​：​只有​ 8 ​份時​，​一項​的​極端值​就​能​主導​總分​（​這是​推論​，​沒​找到​比​較過​合成​方式​的​研究​）。

​項目​ ​指標​ ​方向​ ​依據​ ​不像​提示​ ​和​提示​的​音符​比​對​ F1（​連長​度​一起​比​）＋​節奏​格子​餘弦​相似​度​ ​越低​越​好​ [7][8][6][13] ​不​違規​ ​低音​和​旋律​之間​的​平行​五​八度​（​每個​音​的​比例​）＋​刺耳​重疊​ ​越低​越​好​ [14][15]、​原型​ 02 ​有​變化​、​但​像​真人​ ​小節間​節奏​相似​度​、​音級​熵​、​起音​密度​、​音長​分布​，​各自​離參​考範圍​多遠​ ​越近​越​好​ [5][9][10] ​低音​正確​ ​和弦​換的​時候​，​最低音​是不是​和弦​的​低音​ ​越高越​好​ ​自訂​，​無文獻​依據​

​參考​範圍​從​哪裡​來​（2026-11-22 ​追加​討論​後​決定​：​下一輪​先不放​這一項​）：

  • POP909 ​都​是​ 4/4 ​流行歌​，​風格​不合​。
  • ​用​每格​ 8 ​份候​選​的​中​位數​，​其實​是​「​像​其他​候選​」，8 ​份​都​照抄​時​反而​獎勵​照抄​，​所以​不​採用​。
  • ​古典​方面​有​現成​的​人​聲加​鋼琴​伴奏​語料​：
  • OpenScore Lieder：​約​ 1,300 ​首​ 19 ​世紀​藝術​歌曲​，MusicXML，​專案​方說​明為​ CC0 [29]。
  • When in Rome：​有羅馬​數字​分析​，​可當​和弦​參照​，​但​哪些​ Lieder ​有​分析​還沒​逐首​確認​ [30]。
  • Schubert《​冬之旅​》​資料​集​只有​ 24 ​首​ [31]；Florence Price ​藝術​歌曲​ 112 ​首​（R4 [8]）。
  • ​藝術​歌曲​伴奏​常比​我們​的​目標​繁​複​，​而且​有純​鋼琴​的​前奏​和​間​奏​。​所以​要​先​篩選​曲子​，​例如​民謠​風​的​分節​歌​；​只算​人聲​在​唱​的​小節​；​再驗證​它​能​不能​把​照抄​柱式​和弦​和​好​伴奏​分開​（​這是​推論​，​尚未​試驗​）。
  • ​使用者​決定​：​下一輪​只​實作​不​需​參照​資料​的​門檻​和​排序​，「​像​真人​」​這一項​等​之後用​ Lieder ​做​小​規模​試驗​，​站得住​才​加入​。

​頁​面呈​現​： ​試聽頁​的​每​一格要​列出​每個​候選​在​各項​的​名次​，​並標​出​被​哪​一道​門檻​擋​掉​。​這樣​你​可以​用​耳朵​判斷​指標​選得​對​不​對​。

docs.title: 待解​問題
docs.text:
• ​指標​和​人耳的關​係​： ​建議​下​一輪​讓​你​盲​聽​「​指標​選​的​」vs「​隨機​一份​」，​用十幾格​的​結果​判斷​指標​有​沒​有​幫助​。
  • ​參考​範圍​： ​已​決定​先不放​。​之後用​ OpenScore Lieder ​的​篩選​子集​做​試驗​：​照抄​ prompt ​的​候選要​落​在​範圍​外​，​使用者​聽​了​覺得​好​的​要​落​在​範圍​內​ [29]。
  • ​門檻​值​： ​抄襲​程度​ 0.5、​吻合​率​ 0.7、​空拍​ 25%、​跨度​ 14 ​個​半音​都​是​起始值​，​要​看​第一​輪​結果​再​調​。
  • ​本輪​沒​確認​的​：
  • Yin ​等​人​的​基數​分數​（cardinality score）​公式​ [11]。
  • music21 theoryAnalyzer ​的​用法​。
  • Polyffusion ​和​ GETMusic ​的​評量​定義​。
  • ​一篇​號稱​「​保證​可​演奏​」​的​鋼琴​簡化​論文​（arXiv 2511.16228）​怎麼​定義可​演奏​。

docs.title: Digest A — Harmonic fidelity metrics (r1-1)
docs.text: Decision served: objective metrics for choosing the best of 8 generated symbolic piano accompaniments, given a melody and a FIXED per-beat chord chart. This digest covers only how well each accompaniment realises the chord chart. Run budget: 13 tool calls, 9 sources touched. Accessed: 2026-11-22. All claims come from retrieved pages unless they are tagged [reasoning] or [unverified belief].

docs.title: Findings
docs.text:
• CTnCTR (chord tone to non-chord tone ratio) = (n_c + n_p) / (n_c + n_n). Here n_c is the number of chord tones, n_n the number of non-chord tones, and n_p the "proper" non-chord tones that lie within 2 semitones of the following note. It equals 1 when there are no non-chord tones. Higher is better. It was defined for the MELODY against the chords, not for an accompaniment. | Automatic Melody Harmonization with Triad Chords: A Comparative Study (Yeh et al.) https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.02360 (formula as relayed by search over 2001.02360 / 2202.08423) | Journal of New Music Research 50(1):37–51 (peer-reviewed) | 2021 (arXiv 2020) | accessed 2026-11-22 | med (the PDF could not be parsed, so the formula comes from a search summary, not the paper text) | metric-definition
  • PCS (pitch consonance score): the consonance of intervals between melody notes and chord notes, averaged over 16th-note windows. Unisons, thirds, fifths and sixths count as consonant; seconds, sevenths and tritones as dissonant. MCTD: the duration-weighted mean distance in the 6-D tonal space (Harte et al. 2006) between each melody note's pitch-class vector and its chord label. Lower is better. | Same Yeh et al. paper; descriptions repeated in A Survey on Evaluation Metrics for Music Generation https://arxiv.org/html/2509.00051 and in https://arxiv.org/html/2512.07627 | JNMR (peer-reviewed); the survey and 2512.07627 are arXiv preprints | 2021 / 2025 / 2025 | accessed 2026-11-22 | med | metric-definition
  • Six objective metrics were paired with a 202-participant subjective study. I found no metric-to-rating correlation on the abstract page. A later paper's search snippet reports a "harmonicity" score correlating with CTnCTR (r = 0.90), with PCS (r = 0.88) and with MCTD (r = −0.86). That is a correlation among metrics, not with listeners, and the paper is probably 2202.08423. | https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.02360 ; https://arxiv.org/pdf/2202.08423 | JNMR; arXiv | 2021; 2022 | accessed 2026-11-22 | low (the r values were not seen in the original text, and it is unclear which paper reports them) | empirical-correlation
  • No code repository is linked on the Yeh et al. arXiv page. The later harmonization paper 2512.07627 links https://github.com/NeuraLLMuse/BStarConstraintHarmonization, but it is not stated whether that repo implements the metrics. | https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.02360 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2512.07627 | — | — | accessed 2026-11-22 | med | code-availability
  • Chord Accuracy (CA), original form: CA = 1/(N_tracks·N_chords) · Σ_i Σ_j 1{C_ij = Ĉ_ij}. Chords are recognised per track and per bar from the generated output and compared with the conditioning chords. | PopMAG: Pop Music Accompaniment Generation https://arxiv.org/pdf/2008.07703 (formula via the 2509.00051 survey) | ACM Multimedia 2020 (peer-reviewed) [venue is unverified belief; not confirmed this run] | 2020 | accessed 2026-11-22 | med | metric-definition
  • Chord Accuracy, whole-arrangement form: CA = (1/N_chord) Σ 1{C_i = Ĉ_i}. Chords are extracted from the full generated arrangement with Jiang et al.'s large-vocabulary chord transcription. The match is on root and quality at 1-beat granularity, which the authors call stricter than PopMAG's. The same paper's "Degree of Arrangement" uses KL divergence between pitch-class histograms, but that measures diversity across tracks, not chord fidelity. Subjective results (23 participants, RM-ANOVA) "align" with the objective ones only qualitatively; no correlation is reported. | Structured Multi-Track Accompaniment Arrangement via Style Prior Modelling (Zhao et al.) https://arxiv.org/html/2310.16334v4 | NeurIPS 2024 (peer-reviewed) | 2024 | accessed 2026-11-22 | high | metric-definition
  • No code repo for the system is linked, only a demo page at https://zhaojw1998.github.io/structured-arrangement/. | same | NeurIPS 2024 | 2024 | accessed 2026-11-22 | high | code-availability
  • Piano accompaniment from a lead sheet uses four metrics. (a) Chord Accuracy: exact beat-level match between chords extracted with Dai et al.'s rule-based recogniser and the reference chords. (b) Chord Similarity: cosine similarity of two-bar chord embeddings from a pre-trained chord encoder (Wang et al. 2020, EC²-VAE/poly-dis family), which gives partial credit for shared chord tones. (c) Out-of-key ratio. (d) Grooving similarity. Root, quality and bass handling are not specified. Results on POP909-test, CA/CS in %: ground truth 91.6/95.7, Polyffusion 37.5/54.0, D3PIA 80.1/93.6, WSG-4th (whole-song hierarchical generation) 87.6/94.6, FGG 62.0/77.3. | D3PIA: A Discrete Denoising Diffusion Model for Piano Accompaniment Generation From Lead Sheet (Choi et al., KAIST) https://arxiv.org/html/2602.03523 | arXiv preprint (no venue stated) | 2026-02 | accessed 2026-11-22 | high | metric-definition
  • Evidence that CA/CS and perceived harmony come apart. WSG-4th had higher CA and CS than D3PIA but a lower subjective Harmony rating. Several of its outputs had CS above 0.95 yet were rated about 3 out of 5. The authors attribute this to dissonance and point to its higher out-of-key ratio (2.4% vs 0%). The listening test had 13 participants and 10 excerpts; no correlation statistic is given. Implication: chord-match alone is not sufficient, and an out-of-key or dissonance penalty is needed alongside it. | D3PIA https://arxiv.org/html/2602.03523 | arXiv | 2026 | accessed 2026-11-22 | med (small N, qualitative) | empirical-correlation
  • Code: training code and samples are stated to be on https://jech2.github.io/D3PIA/. The Polyffusion code is at https://github.com/aik2mlj/polyffusion (ISMIR 2023). | D3PIA; Polyffusion https://arxiv.org/pdf/2307.10304 | arXiv; ISMIR 2023 (peer-reviewed) | 2026; 2023 | accessed 2026-11-22 | med | code-availability
  • Chroma similarity per bar: s_chr = 100·⟨r^a, r^b⟩ / (‖r^a‖‖r^b‖), where r is a 12-dimensional chroma vector of onset counts. To use it for chord fidelity, take r^b as the chord-template chroma [reasoning]. | A Survey on Evaluation Metrics for Music Generation https://arxiv.org/html/2509.00051 (attributes it to Wang et al. 2024) | arXiv survey | 2025 | accessed 2026-11-22 | med | metric-definition
  • The survey reports NO human-correlation evidence for any symbolic harmony metric (CTnCTR, PCS, MCTD, CA, TD, PCH entropy). Its validated-correlation results concern audio metrics only (FAD, KAD, MAD). It warns that feature metrics are "no way sufficient" for overall quality. | https://arxiv.org/html/2509.00051 | arXiv | 2025 | accessed 2026-11-22 | high | empirical-correlation
  • Other harmony suites appear in accompaniment papers. SongDriver uses chord pitch interval, CTnCTR, melody-chord consonance and chord stability. ReaLchords uses the note-in-chord ratio. | https://arxiv.org/pdf/2209.06054 ; https://arxiv.org/pdf/2506.14723 (search summaries only) | arXiv (SongDriver: ACM MM 2022 [unverified belief]) | 2022; 2025 | accessed 2026-11-22 | low | metric-definition
  • Sparse output [reasoning, not evidenced in sources]:
  • Chord-tone ratios (CTR, CTnCTR) and PCS are normalised by note count. An accompaniment of a few sustained chord tones therefore scores close to perfect, so these metrics reward sparse or blocky output.
  • Recogniser-based CA/CS should penalise very sparse output on beats with too few notes to recognise, but they reward root-position block chords.
  • Pair them with a density or texture term, or with a coverage term: the fraction of chord-chart beats where the chord's pitch classes are actually present.

docs.title: Bass / root on downbeats (Q3)
docs.text:
• Root is matched, but there is no separate bass or inversion criterion. The only retrieved metric that states its matching criterion (Zhao et al., NeurIPS 2024) compares root + quality. Root here means the chord-label root, not the sounding bass note. D3PIA does not specify root/quality/bass handling. | high | metric-definition
  • I found no published bass-correctness or root-on-downbeat metric for accompaniment generation in this run (see "Looked for but not found").
  • [reasoning] A large-vocabulary recogniser such as Jiang et al. outputs inversions (e.g. C/E), so whether bass matters depends on whether slash chords are collapsed before comparison. Wrong-bass realisations of a chart are perceptually salient. For a fixed chart, a simple custom metric (the lowest sounding pitch class on each chart-chord onset equals the chart's bass or root) is cheap to add, but it is unvalidated.

docs.title: Leads worth chasing
docs.text:
• Read Yeh et al. JNMR 2021 itself (DOI under 10.1080/09298215.2021.x) to confirm the exact CTnCTR, PCS and MCTD formulas and whether any metric–listener correlation is reported.
  • The Whole-Song Hierarchical Generation paper (Wang, Min, Xia, ICLR 2024; "WSG"): check its chord evaluation and code (likely in the ZZWaang GitHub repos) [unverified belief].
  • The Dai et al. rule-based chord extractor used by D3PIA, and the Jiang et al. large-vocabulary chord transcription: confirm code availability. These would serve as the recogniser that turns a generated accompaniment into a chord sequence to compare with the chart.
  • Wang et al. 2020 chord encoder (poly-dis / EC²-VAE): reuse it for the Chord Similarity metric.
  • FIGARO (von Rütte et al., ICLR 2023) "chord accuracy" description metric; GETMusic; AccoMontage / AccoMontage2 chord evaluation. None were fetched this run.
  • "Local chord corruption is not recognizer replay" (arXiv 2609.03584, preprint, code at https://github.com/Viwennnnnn/local-chord-corruption-replay) argues that response magnitude and output-chord agreement should be reported together. It is tangential: audio, MIDI-SAG and MusicGen-Chord.
  • Accompaniment Prompt Adherence (arXiv 2503.06346) is validated against human judgments, but it is audio and CLAP-based.

docs.title: Looked for but not found
docs.text:
• Any published Pearson or Spearman correlation between a symbolic chord-fidelity metric (CA, CS, CTR, CTnCTR, MCTD) and listener ratings of accompaniments.
  • A bass-correctness, root-presence or downbeat-root metric in a 2021–2026 accompaniment paper.
  • A Tonal Pitch Space (Lerdahl) chord-similarity metric used for accompaniment evaluation. Only the Harte 6-D tonal-centroid distance appeared.
  • Code for the Yeh et al. metrics (no repo was linked on the arXiv page).
  • The Polyffusion chord-accuracy definition: the ISMIR 2023 paper text was not fetched, and the search snippets did not show the column definitions.

docs.title: AB leads, round 2, part 1: exact metric definitions
docs.text:
The question these metrics serve: which objective metrics should rank 8 generated symbolic piano accompaniments, given a melody and a fixed chord chart? The generator is conditioned on block chords and sometimes just replays them.

Method: I fetched the arXiv PDFs, pulled out their text locally with macOS PDFKit, and searched it. I read mir_eval's source as raw text from GitHub. All accessed 2026-11-22.

docs.title: Findings
docs.text:
• Yeh et al., CTnCTR (Eq. 11). CTnCTR = (n_c + n_p) / (n_c + n_n).
  • Chord tones (n_c) are melody notes whose pitch class is in the current triad for that half-bar. All other melody notes are non-chord tones (n_n).
  • n_p counts "proper" non-chord tones: those "two semitones within the notes which are right after them".
  • The value equals 1 when there are no non-chord tones, or when n_p = n_n.
  • Source: Automatic Melody Harmonization with Triad Chords: A Comparative Study, https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.02360 | JNMR (arXiv preprint) | 2020-01 (arXiv v1) | accessed 2026-11-22 | high | primary-text.
  • Yeh et al., PCS. Each melody note is scored against each of the 3 chord notes, with the melody assumed to be above the chord.
  • Score +1 for unison, major/minor 3rd, perfect 5th and major/minor 6th. Score 0 for a perfect 4th. Score -1 for any other interval.
  • The scores are averaged over 16th-note windows, excluding rests.
  • Human-composed reference values: CTnCTR 0.74, PCS 1.42, MCTD 1.03.
  • Caveat: template matching scores higher than human on CTnCTR and PCS (0.91, 1.97). So "higher" is not "better", and chord replay would likely be over-rewarded.
  • Source: same | high | primary-text.
  • Yeh et al., MCTD. Each melody note becomes a one-hot PCP (pitch-class profile) vector. Its distance to the chord's PCP is measured in the 6-D tonal space of Harte et al. 2006. MCTD is the average of these distances, weighted by each melody note's duration.
  • The authors advise using the metrics "to gain practical insights … rather than to judge their quality".
  • Source: same | high | primary-text.
  • mir_eval transcription defaults. precision_recall_f1_overlap and match_notes use onset_tolerance=0.05 s, pitch_tolerance=50 cents, offset_ratio=0.2, offset_min_tolerance=0.05 s, strict=False. precision_recall_f1_overlap also has beta=1.0.
  • Offset window = max(0.2 × reference duration, 50 ms).
  • Notes are paired by bipartite maximum matching, not greedy matching.
  • offset_ratio=None ignores offsets (reported as the _no_offset scores).
  • Separate onset-only and offset-only P/R/F functions ignore pitch.
  • Average overlap ratio = overlap time / (latest offset − earliest onset), averaged over matched pairs.
  • Source: mir_eval/transcription.py, https://github.com/craffel/mir_eval/blob/main/mir_eval/transcription.py | official source code | main branch | accessed 2026-11-22 | high (read via a summarizing fetch of the raw source, not line by line) | primary-code.
  • FIGARO, description fidelity (Sec. 5.2, App. D).
  • Categorical features: mean F1 for instruments and for chords (multi-label), plain accuracy for time signature. The table calls the chord metric "chord F1-score (C)", not "chord accuracy".
  • Note density: bar-wise NRMSE = RMSE(x, x̂) / mean(x).
  • Pitch, velocity and duration: Macro Overlapping Area (MOA). For each bar, fit a Gaussian to the feature in each sequence and take the overlapping area. MOA is the mean over the N bars. It fixes the problem that whole-piece OA (overlapping area) is maximal even for a reversed sequence.
  • Chroma and grooving similarity: bar-wise cosine similarity, following Wu & Yang 2021. Grooving vectors follow Dixon et al. 2004.
  • Source: FIGARO: Generating Symbolic Music with Fine-Grained Artistic Control, https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.10936 | ICLR 2023 | 2023 | accessed 2026-11-22 | high | primary-text.
  • Whole-Song Hierarchical Generation, ILS (Sec. 5.3, Table 2). ILS (inter-phrase latent similarity) is computed from a cosine-similarity matrix over 2-bar segments in a pretrained VAE latent space.
  • The ratio is the average similarity of same-label phrases over the average similarity of all phrases. Higher means more structure.
  • Variants: ILS_p and ILS_r (EC2-VAE pitch and rhythm latents of the melody), ILS_chd (chord latent), ILS_txt (accompaniment texture latent from Wang et al. 2020b).
  • Ground-truth ILS_txt = 1.68.
  • Source: Whole-Song Hierarchical Generation of Symbolic Music Using Cascaded Diffusion Models, https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.09901 | ICLR 2024 | 2024-05 (arXiv) | accessed 2026-11-22 | high | primary-text.
  • Whole-Song, control efficacy (App. D, Table 6). For each stage (chord, rhythm, texture), they report a rule-based distance dis_rb (lower is better) and a latent similarity sim_lt (higher is better) between the generated output and the external control.
  • This is the closest thing in these papers to a faithfulness-to-condition metric for texture. I did not get the exact formula for dis_rb.
  • Source: same | medium | primary-text.
  • Whole-Song, Degree of Copying (memorization appendix). sim_rb(x, x′) = 2·n_{x∩x′} / (n_x + n_x′), where the intersection counts notes with the same pitch class and the same onset.
  • S(x) ∈ [0, 1], and the histogram of S(x) is reported as mean ± standard deviation. A latent version uses EC2-VAE to catch indirect copying of contour or rhythm.
  • This could be used as a chord-replay detector: compute sim_rb between the generated accompaniment and the block-chord condition. That is my inference.
  • Source: same | high (formula) | primary-text.
  • AccoMontage, phrase matching (Sec. 3.2). The fitness score is the cosine similarity of rhythm features plus the cosine similarity of TIV-mapped chroma. Rhythm features are 3-D (onset, hold, rest). TIV is the 12-D Tonal Interval Vector.
  • The form term treats phrases as matching when their step-wise cosine similarity is > 0.99.
  • Evaluation is subjective only, on a 5-point scale for Coherence (fits the melody in harmony and texture), Structure and Musicality. I found no objective texture metric in the extracted text.
  • Source: AccoMontage: Accompaniment Arrangement via Phrase Selection and Style Transfer, https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.11213 | ISMIR 2021 | 2021 | accessed 2026-11-22 | medium-high | primary-text.
  • Yin et al., originality report (partial). The Springer paper (SN Computer Science, s42979-022-01220-y) defines an "originality report" with a parameterised similarity score, and uses a cardinality score and a fingerprinting score as case studies.
  • Not confirmed this run: that the cardinality score is a translation-invariant point-set match (the maximum number of points shared under a translation, normalized by set size). This is an unverified belief.
  • Not confirmed this run: the author list and the code location.
  • Source: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s42979-022-01220-y | SN Computer Science | 2022 | accessed 2026-11-22 | low (search snippet only) | secondary-snippet.

docs.title: Leads
docs.text:
• Yin et al.: fetch the Springer full text (open access?) to get the cardinality-score formula and the code link (possibly a GitHub repo by Z. Yin, unverified).
  • Whole-Song App. D: get the exact dis_rb definitions for texture and rhythm control.
  • FIGARO App. D.3: get the exact grooving-vector definition and the code, which is in the FIGARO GitHub repo (unverified).
  • Polyffusion: the arXiv PDF was fetched (2307.10304), but searching the extracted text for "accuracy", "chord accuracy" and "overlapping area" found nothing. The metrics may be named differently, or the extraction may be faulty. Re-read Sec. 4/5 directly.
  • For replay detection, Whole-Song's sim_rb applied to accompaniment vs. block chords looks like the simplest ready-made definition.

docs.title: Looked for but not found
docs.text:
• GETMusic (2023) objective metrics: not fetched (tool budget).
  • Polyffusion chord accuracy definition: not found in the extracted text (see Leads).
  • A "faithfulness vs creativity" metric pair in AccoMontage or FIGARO: none found. Whole-Song's DoC/memorization analysis and its control-efficacy table come closest.
  • A rhythm/texture diversity metric (a diversity measure across samples) in any of the 5 papers: not found. FIGARO grooving similarity and Whole-Song ILS_txt measure similarity, not diversity.

docs.title: Digest B: prompt-copy / similarity / texture metrics (r1-1)
docs.text: Scope: objective metrics to penalise a generated piano accompaniment that replays the block-chord conditioning prompt, while still allowing partial reuse. Accessed 2026-11-22. Tool budget ran out (12 calls). Two PDFs could not be parsed (no PDF renderer), so several formulas below come only from search-result summaries. Those are flagged.

docs.title: Findings
docs.text:
• Grooving pattern similarity (GS): a bar's onset grid is a binary vector g ∈ {0,1}^64. GS(g_a, g_b) = 1 − (1/Q)·Σ_q XOR(g_a[q], g_b[q]), with Q = 64, so the range is [0,1]. Proposed as a within-piece rhythmicity measure. Applied as GS(candidate bar, block-chord prompt bar), it scores how closely the candidate's onsets match the prompt's. A block-chord prompt has onsets only at chord changes, so a high GS means the candidate copies the prompt's rhythm. | "The Jazz Transformer on the Front Line" (Wu & Yang) https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.01307 | ISMIR 2020 (peer-reviewed; venue confirmed on the arXiv abs page) | 2020 | accessed 2026-11-22 | confidence: medium (formula comes from the search snippet of the PDF; I could not read the PDF text) | class: metric-definition
  • Pitfall: XOR counts shared silences as matches. A very sparse candidate scored against a sparse block-chord prompt gets a high GS, and a dense random candidate gets a low GS (it looks "original"). Use it with an onset-density floor and ceiling. The arXiv page links no code: unverified whether official code exists.
  • GS variants: MIDI-RWKV restates GS as the average share of onset positions (present or absent) that match, credited to Wu & Yang 2020. A 2026 piano-arrangement paper uses 4-bar segments at 1/4-beat resolution and cosine similarity instead of XOR, averaged over non-overlapping segments. Cosine ignores shared silences, which reduces the sparse-output pitfall. | "Adaptable Symbolic Music Infilling with MIDI-RWKV" https://arxiv.org/pdf/2506.13001 ; "Learning Music Style for Piano Arrangement Through Cross-Modal Bootstrapping" https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.03050 | arXiv preprints | 2025 / 2026 | accessed 2026-11-22 | confidence: medium (from search summary) | class: metric-definition
  • mgeval feature set: pitch count, pitch-class histogram, pitch-class transition matrix (PCTM), pitch range, average pitch interval, note count, average inter-onset interval (IOI), note-length histogram, note-length transition matrix. It also supports "relative metrics" that compare two sets (e.g. training vs generated). Note count, IOI and the note-length histogram/transition matrix are direct texture-vs-block-chord signals: block chords give long, uniform note lengths and a large IOI equal to the chord duration. | mgeval README https://github.com/RichardYang40148/mgeval ; paper "On the evaluation of generative models in music" DOI 10.1007/s00521-018-3849-7 | Neural Computing and Applications (Springer journal, peer-reviewed) | 2018 online / 2020 issue | accessed 2026-11-22 | confidence: high for the feature list, low for the OA/KLD formulas (the README does not show them) | class: metric-definition, code-availability
  • Overlapping Area (OA) = ∫ min(p_A(x), p_B(x)) dx between kernel-density estimates of a feature's intra-set and inter-set distance distributions, plus KL divergence. Unverified belief: not confirmed this run. The README points to mgeval/documentation.md, which I did not fetch. OA is defined between sets, not for a single pair, so it does not fit per-candidate scoring of 8 outputs unless you treat each candidate's bars as a set.
  • Originality report: measures how much a generator copies compared with a baseline of how much human composers borrow from themselves and each other. Their Transformer fell below the baseline's 95% CI. Overfitting in later training epochs produced copies of input excerpts. Data and code are on OSF. | Yin et al., "Measuring When a Music Generation Algorithm Copies Too Much: The Originality Report, Cardinality Score, and Symbolic Fingerprinting by Geometric Hashing" https://eprints.whiterose.ac.uk/190005/ (Springer DOI 10.1007/s42979-022-01220-y) | SN Computer Science (peer-reviewed journal) | 2022 | accessed 2026-11-22 | confidence: medium (from search summary; full text could not be parsed) | class: metric-definition, empirical-correlation, code-availability
  • Cardinality score, likely mechanism (unverified belief): the largest number of (onset, pitch) points shared under a translation in time and pitch, divided by the size of the excerpt. Because block chords are a point set, this would give a direct "fraction of prompt notes reproduced" with transposition and shift invariance. Pitfall (unverified): the score drops for random or sparse output, so on its own it rewards noise. Calibrate against a human-accompaniment baseline, as the paper does.
  • SSIMuse: adapts the image Structural Similarity Index to symbolic piano-rolls to detect replication between generated and training pieces. Aimed at textured and expressive music that melody-focused measures handle poorly. It could compare a candidate piano-roll with the rendered block-chord piano-roll locally, catching shared notes and sustained durations at once. | Ji et al. https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.13658 | arXiv preprint | 2025-09 | accessed 2026-11-22 | confidence: medium (from search summary) | class: metric-definition
  • Motif-level plagiarism: plagiarism-like outputs from Transformer symbolic models are linked to local overfitting on frequently repeated motifs. Proposed fixes are label smoothing, transposition augmentation and Top-K sampling. Context for why a model replays its prompt. | Inaba & Inui, "Why Do Music Models Plagiarize? A Motif-Centric Perspective" https://neurips.cc/virtual/2025/123788 | NeurIPS 2025 workshop (light peer review) | 2025 | accessed 2026-11-22 | confidence: medium | class: empirical-correlation
  • Rhythm similarity vs perception: the GrooveToolbox paper proposes new rhythm-similarity metrics for drum loops. A structural rhythmic similarity measure correlated more strongly with perceived similarity than the commonly used Hamming distance (which is essentially the XOR in GS). This suggests a GS score may not match what listeners hear as similar. | GrooveToolbox thesis / paper https://duo.uio.no/handle/10852/84395 | thesis/repository, venue unverified | 2021 | accessed 2026-11-22 | confidence: low-medium | class: empirical-correlation
  • mir_eval note precision/recall/F: a note matches if the onset is within ±50 ms and the pitch within ±50 cents, with an optional offset criterion (within max(50 ms, 0.2 × reference duration)). An onset-only variant exists, plus an overlap-ratio score. This gives per-candidate copy rate = recall of prompt notes among candidate notes, and precision = share of candidate notes that are prompt copies. Unverified belief: the docs URL returned 404 this run. Recalled from training data; module mir_eval.transcription, functions precision_recall_f1_overlap and onset_precision_recall_f1, are unverified. | https://github.com/craffel/mir_eval (not fetched) | Raffel et al., ISMIR 2014 (peer-reviewed, unverified this run) | — | accessed 2026-11-22 | confidence: low | class: metric-definition
  • Pitfall: block chords are sustained, so a candidate that restrikes the same chord notes on every beat gets low offset-aware F but high onset-only recall at chord changes. Compute both onset-only and offset-aware scores and penalise the offset-aware match most heavily ("same notes, same onsets/durations"). Empty output gets precision 0/0, so define it as maximal penalty.

docs.title: Synthesis (my inference, not from a single source)
docs.text:
A copy penalty that allows partial reuse could combine: - (a) offset-aware note F1 against the block-chord render, penalised only above a threshold such as 0.3; - (b) GS (cosine variant) between candidate and prompt onset grids; - (c) texture guards from the mgeval features: onset density relative to chord changes (onsets per chord span > 1), sustained-note ratio (share of notes lasting ≥ the chord span), and note-length histogram entropy.

Pair each with floors for note count and onset density so that sparse or random output is not rewarded.

docs.title: Leads worth chasing
docs.text:
• mgeval documentation.md for the exact OA/KLD implementation (https://github.com/RichardYang40148/mgeval).
  • Yin et al. 2022 full text and OSF code for the cardinality score and geometric-hashing fingerprint. This is likely the best ready-made "partial copy" detector.
  • Jazz Transformer text (arXiv 2008.01307) for the exact GS formula and the related "chord progression irregularity" and "structureness indicator" (SI) metrics. The SI uses self-similarity matrices.
  • The 2026 piano-arrangement paper (arXiv 2608.03050), which may define accompaniment-texture metrics directly.
  • MuseGAN (Dong et al., AAAI 2018) metrics "polyphonicity" and "qualified note rate" as texture signals. Not searched this run.

docs.title: Looked for but not found (this run)
docs.text:
• No metric explicitly defined as "similarity to the conditioning prompt" in accompaniment generation; the copy metrics found compare against training data.
  • No published "sustained-note ratio" or "onset density relative to chord changes" metric was retrieved. These are proposed here (inference).
  • mir_eval transcription docs (404) and both PDFs (could not be parsed) were not verified.

docs.title: C-leads round 2, part 1: rule-violation and playability checks (best-of-8 piano accompaniment)
docs.text: Brief: objective rule-violation and playability checks on symbolic MIDI (melody and chord chart given). Web only. 14 tool calls. Several PDFs (arXiv 2107.10388, CMMR 2023 zenodo) could not be parsed because no local PDF tool was available, so I could not read them.

docs.title: Findings
docs.text:
• Correction to the brief. The authors of "Bach or Mock?" are Alexander Fang, Alisa Liu, Prem Seetharaman and Bryan Pardo. No "Lin" is listed. The venue is the ML4MD Workshop at ICML 2020, a 2-page paper. | arXiv abs page https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.13329 | ICML 2020 ML4MD workshop | 2020-06-23 (v3 2020-07-17) | accessed 2026-11-22 | high | bibliographic
  • Bach or Mock features. There are six feature distributions: (1) pitch, as scale degrees with spelling kept and octave ignored; (2) rhythm, as durations in quarter-note units; (3) directed melodic intervals, with one distribution for each of S, A, T and B; (4) harmonic quality, as chord-quality distribution; (5) parallel errors, as counts of parallel 5ths, 8ves and unisons in similar and contrary motion; (6) lengths of repeated note sequences (Hsu et al. 1998). Voice crossing is not a feature. | arXiv HTML v3 https://arxiv.org/html/2006.13329v3 | ICML 2020 ML4MD | 2020 | accessed 2026-11-22 | high | method
  • How Bach or Mock combines them. It is built on music21. For each feature it takes the Wasserstein distance from the reference distribution of the Bach corpus. The grade is a weighted sum of those distances (weights are mostly 1), and lower is better. The parallel-error term is scaled by (the piece's error-to-note ratio) / (Bach's ratio). That per-note normalisation can be reused directly for counting violations across 8 candidates. | same | | 2020 | accessed 2026-11-22 | high | method
  • Bach or Mock validation. Median grade was 4.91 for Bach and 8.94 for generated chorales. On 3 paired discriminations, the grader picked the Bach chorale 92% of the time, against 86.7% for "experts". There were 36 listeners, but only 5 experts. This is a discrimination task, not a correlation with quality ratings. | same | | 2020 | accessed 2026-11-22 | medium (small n) | evidence
  • Bach or Mock code. Code exists at https://github.com/asdfang/constraint-transformer-bach/tree/master/Grader. I did not inspect it. | arXiv HTML v3 | | 2020 | accessed 2026-11-22 | high (that it exists) | code
  • Coconet / Bach Doodle. The authors examined parallel 5ths and 8ves in Coconet output. They found such parallels were common in the training data, and with no key or time signatures in that data the model probably learned them as acceptable. Note the caveat: a raw parallel count can flag patterns that exist in the reference corpus itself. I saw this only in a search snippet and did not read the paper. | "The Bach Doodle…" https://arxiv.org/pdf/1907.06637 | arXiv / ISMIR 2019 | 2019 | accessed 2026-11-22 | medium | evidence
  • CMMR 2023 paper. It adds a training loss that penalises prohibited patterns such as parallel 5ths and 8ves. I could not read the title, authors or numbers. | https://zenodo.org/records/10112462/files/cmmr2023_2c-P5.pdf | CMMR 2023 | 2023 | accessed 2026-11-22 | low | lead
  • music21 voiceLeading.VoiceLeadingQuartet(v1n1, v1n2, v2n1, v2n2, key). Voice 1 is the upper voice. It provides parallelFifth() (which includes antiparallel fifths and fifths displaced by an octave), parallelOctave(), parallelUnison(), parallelUnisonOrOctave(), parallelInterval(), hiddenFifth() and hiddenOctave() (the docs say these find all hidden intervals, not only the forbidden ones), voiceCrossing() and voiceOverlap(). Documented helper: iterateAllVoiceLeadingQuartets(). It works on pairs of monophonic voice lines, so piano chords must first be split into lines. | music21 voiceLeading docs https://music21.org/music21docs/moduleReference/moduleVoiceLeading.html | official docs | current | accessed 2026-11-22 | high | tool
  • music21 theoryAnalyzer. The docs say only that theoryAnalyzer "divides a score up into these segments" of VLQ objects. I could not confirm the identifyParallelFifths signature: the docs page does not list it and the raw GitHub path returned 404. Unverified belief: it lives in music21.alpha.theoryAnalysis.theoryAnalyzer, takes partNum pairs and stores results via addAnalysisData. music21.figuredBass.checker also exists as source and is a likely alternative. | music21 docs (above); search result https://music21.org/music21docs/_modules/music21/figuredBass/checker.html | | | accessed 2026-11-22 | low | tool
  • McLeod & Steedman HMM voice separation. Published in JNMR 2016. It separates MIDI, including live performance MIDI, into monophonic voices and was evaluated on Bach pieces against voices taken from the score. Code and data are at https://github.com/apmcleod/voice-splitting. Their 2018 paper notes there is no standard voice-separation metric and uses average voice consistency and precision/recall/F1. Chew & Wu (2005) and Jordanous (2008) are the baselines compared. | "HMM-Based Voice Separation of MIDI Performance" https://www.research.ed.ac.uk/en/publications/hmm-based-voice-separation-of-midi-performance/ ; ISMIR 2018 https://ismir2018.ismir.net/doc/pdfs/148_Paper.pdf | JNMR 2016; ISMIR 2018 | 2016/2018 | accessed 2026-11-22 | medium (snippets) | tool/evidence
  • Ramoneda piano difficulty. The ICASSP 2022 paper is "Score difficulty analysis for piano performance education based on fingering". It estimates difficulty from predicted fingering, not from explicit hand-span features. The follow-up "Combining piano performance dimensions for score difficulty classification" (ESWA 2024, doi 10.1016/j.eswa.2023.121776; arXiv 2306.08480) uses pretrained fingering and expressiveness models on the CIPI dataset: 652 pieces, 9 levels, 39.5% balanced accuracy. These are learned embeddings and give no explicit hand-span, chord-size or speed thresholds. | UPF repository https://repositori.upf.edu/handle/10230/53378 ; https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2306.08480 | ICASSP 2022; ESWA 2024 | 2022/2024 | accessed 2026-11-22 | medium | evidence
  • Difficulty-controlled piano simplification (arXiv 2511.16228, 2025). The authors say their transformer output "guarantees playability" and they release the PianoPairs dataset. How they define playability was not retrieved. | https://arxiv.org/html/2511.16228v1 | arXiv | 2025-11 | accessed 2026-11-22 | low | lead

docs.title: Leads
docs.text:
• Read Grader/ in asdfang/constraint-transformer-bach. It is the reference implementation for counting parallel errors with music21 and normalising per note.
  • arXiv 2511.16228: find its playability definition. It may contain explicit hand-span or polyphony rules.
  • arXiv 2408.00473 ("Towards Explainable and Interpretable Musical [difficulty]…", Ramoneda group?) may contain explicit interpretable difficulty features.
  • arXiv 2107.10388 (JS Fake Chorales): listeners were near chance. Check whether it reports any rule counts.
  • ISMIR 2017 paper 000026 and de Valk's thesis (City, Univ. London) on voice separation came up in the search and were not read.
  • music21 figuredBass.checker source: possibly a ready-made checker for parallels across parts.

docs.title: Looked for but not found
docs.text:
• Explicit hand-span, chord-size or speed features in the Ramoneda papers. None appeared in what I retrieved; their work uses learned fingering embeddings.
  • A validated skyline-algorithm baseline for extracting outer voices from piano MIDI. No source retrieved. Unverified belief: for piano accompaniment, taking the highest and lowest sounding note per onset (skyline and "floor") is the simplest way to get the outer voices. No validation evidence was retrieved this run.
  • Studies linking rule-violation counts to listening ratings for TonicNet, DeepBach or BachBot (2021–2025). None were retrieved. Only Bach or Mock's discrimination accuracy is evidenced.
  • VoSA; Chew & Wu contig mapping details (it appeared only as a baseline name).
  • The signature and documentation of music21 theoryAnalyzer.identifyParallelFifths (404 / not indexed).

docs.title: C: Harmony / voice-leading rule violations and piano playability (round 1, agent 1)
docs.text: Accessed 2026-11-22. Web search/fetch only. 13 tool calls. Some claims come from search-result summaries rather than full-text reads; those are marked "snippet-level".

docs.title: Voice-leading / part-writing checkers
docs.text:
• music21 voiceLeading.VoiceLeadingQuartet (two voices x two time points) has booleans for every core rule: parallelFifth() (parallel or antiparallel P5, octave displacement allowed), parallelOctave(), parallelUnison(), parallelUnisonOrOctave(), hiddenFifth(), hiddenOctave(), hiddenInterval(), voiceCrossing(), voiceOverlap(), isProperResolution() (dissonant P4/A4/d5/m7 resolve correctly), leapNotSetWithStep(), and motion types (parallel/similar/contrary/oblique). There is NO dedicated leading-tone or chordal-7th resolution method; isProperResolution covers the interval-level case only. Spacing checks were not seen in this module. Verticality.isConsonant() and ThreeNoteLinearSegment.couldBePassingTone()/couldBeNeighborTone() are also there. | music21 voiceLeading module docs, https://music21.org/music21docs/moduleReference/moduleVoiceLeading.html | official docs (MIT, open-source) | current docs | accessed 2026-11-22 | high | tool / code-availability
  • Applying it to piano texture: the quartet API needs explicit voice pairs, so a non-4-voice piano accompaniment first needs voice separation (e.g. outer voices = bass and top note per onset, then pair bass with melody). That is the usual approach, but I found no evidence-backed recipe this run. | — | — | — | — | unverified belief | metric-definition
  • "Bach or Mock? A Grading Function for Chorales in the Style of J.S. Bach" (Fang, Liu, Seetharaman, Pardo) offers an interpretable grading function for four-part chorales that scores "important musical features". The authors report it separates Bach from model-generated chorales better than human experts. The abstract does not list the rules. Code was not found on the arXiv page. | https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.13329 | ML4MD Workshop @ ICML 2020 (workshop, not a full peer-reviewed paper) | 2020-06 | accessed 2026-11-22 | medium | metric-definition / empirical-correlation
  • Peyser, a Princeton student independent-work report, built a Bach-style chorale checker that flags style violations and writes a report. It says no full checker existed at the time. | https://www.cs.princeton.edu/~rdondero/iw/12Peyser.pdf | undergraduate report (not peer-reviewed) | ~2012 | accessed 2026-11-22 | low (snippet-level) | tool
  • An ICCS 2022 melody-harmonization paper scores candidate harmonizations with a fitness function built from music-theory rules, which is a precedent for a "rule-violation count" score. | https://www.iccs-meeting.org/archive/iccs2022/papers/133500022.pdf | ICCS 2022 (peer-reviewed conference) | 2022 | accessed 2026-11-22 | low (snippet-level) | metric-definition
  • A weighted-rule chorale model (Bach-estimated weights) is a precedent for weighting rules by corpus frequency instead of treating them as hard rules. | https://muse.jhu.edu/article/760051/pdf | journal on Project MUSE (peer-reviewed; exact title not verified) | — | accessed 2026-11-22 | low (snippet-level) | metric-definition
  • The Bach Doodle paper (Coconet) came up for the voice-leading query. Whether it counts parallel-5th/8ve violations was not verified this run. | https://arxiv.org/pdf/1907.06637 | ISMIR 2019 | 2019 | accessed 2026-11-22 | low | lead

docs.title: Dissonance / consonance / tension
docs.text:
• Harrison & Pearce test 20 consonance models and argue that consonance is composite: interference (roughness), periodicity/harmonicity, and cultural familiarity. They propose a composite model and a corpus-familiarity model. The R package incon implements 17 models (e.g. Hutchinson-Knopoff roughness, harmonicity, corpus, composite). It takes symbolic pitch sets as input, so it can score each chord in a MIDI accompaniment. | "Simultaneous Consonance in Music Perception and Composition", https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7032667 ; code https://github.com/pmcharrison/incon (README https://rdrr.io/github/pmcharrison/incon/f/README.md) | Psychological Review (peer-reviewed) | 2020 | accessed 2026-11-22 | high | metric-definition / tool / code-availability
  • Caveat: an independent poster (U. Minnesota) found surprisingly large disagreements between consonance models on dyads. Which model you pick matters, so report more than one. | https://conservancy.umn.edu/bitstream/handle/11299/223045/poster_final_final.pdf | poster (not peer-reviewed) | — | accessed 2026-11-22 | low (snippet-level) | empirical-correlation
  • Herremans & Chew "Tension Ribbons" compute three tonal-tension measures on the Spiral Array over sliding windows. Cloud diameter is the maximal distance between notes in the window, i.e. dissonance. Cloud momentum is the movement of the window's center of effect, i.e. tonal change. Tensile strain is the distance of the center of effect from the key. MorpheuS uses them as generation targets. The one-line definitions come from my memory of the paper, and the retrieved page only names the three measures, so treat the definitions as partly unverified. | https://dorienherremans.com/content/tension-ribbons-quantifying-and-visualising-tonal-tension ; preprint https://www.dorienherremans.com/sites/default/files/paper_tenor_dh_preprint_small.pdf | TENOR 2016 (peer-reviewed conference) | 2016 | accessed 2026-11-22 | medium | metric-definition
  • Sensory dissonance in Essentia is audio-only. For symbolic input you have to synthesize partials and apply Sethares/Plomp-Levelt yourself, or use incon. | search summary (Essentia docs not fetched) | — | — | accessed 2026-11-22 | low | tool

docs.title: Piano playability
docs.text:
• PIG dataset + statistical fingering (Nakamura, Saito, Yoshii): about 150 classical pieces with pianist fingerings, plus high-order HMM / DNN fingering estimators. A fingering model's likelihood or cost per note can serve as a difficulty or playability proxy. That use is my inference, not something the paper claims. | "Statistical Learning and Estimation of Piano Fingering", https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.10237 ; demo https://statpianofingering.github.io/demo.html | Information Sciences 2020 (journal version: unverified belief); arXiv 2019 | 2019-04 | accessed 2026-11-22 | high (dataset/method); low (proxy use) | tool / code-availability
  • ThumbSet (Ramoneda et al. 2022) is a larger, noisier fingering set. Pretraining on it and then fine-tuning on PIG beats the HMM baselines. | https://zenodo.org/records/6433702 | dataset (Zenodo) | 2022-04 | accessed 2026-11-22 | medium | tool
  • RubricNet (Ramoneda et al.) is an interpretable symbolic piano-difficulty model on the CIPI dataset (652 pieces, 9 levels). Its descriptors are computed per hand. Pitch entropy is the Shannon entropy of pitches. Pitch range is max minus min MIDI pitch. Average pitch is mean MIDI pitch. Displacement rate is the weighted mean of the largest jump between consecutive pitch-set events (weight 0 under 7 semitones, 1 from 7 to 11, 2 from 12 up). Average IOI is in seconds, with 100 bpm assumed if no tempo. Pitch-set LZ is Lempel-Ziv complexity. It does NOT use hand span, polyphony or fingering cost. Code: https://github.com/pramoneda/rubricnet | "Towards Explainable and Interpretable Musical Difficulty Estimation", https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.00473 | arXiv preprint (search summary says ISMIR 2024; not verified on page) | 2024-08 | accessed 2026-11-22 | high | metric-definition / code-availability
  • Ghatas, Fayek & Hadhoud split piano rolls into segments and train a hybrid DL classifier for difficulty. It is a black box, so it is less useful as an interpretable penalty. | https://doaj.org/article/d2a9c34b038643b5bf69cd32bc48ba2a | Alexandria Engineering Journal (peer-reviewed) | 2022-12 | accessed 2026-11-22 | medium | empirical-correlation
  • Predicting difficulty from sheet images (Ramoneda et al.) and audio (the PSyllabus dataset, 7,901 pieces, 11 levels) are not directly applicable to MIDI. | https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.16287 ; https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.03947 | arXiv / ISMIR-adjacent | 2023-2024 | accessed 2026-11-22 | medium | lead
  • Accompaniment-generation papers (AccoMontage2, Florence Price art-song generator) evaluate with listening tests and perceived-error counts. The Price paper reports 45% error-free generations. Neither reports an automatic playability metric in the retrieved summaries. | https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.00353 ; https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.23130 | ISMIR 2022 / arXiv 2025 | — | accessed 2026-11-22 | medium (snippet-level) | empirical-correlation
  • Simple hard-constraint heuristics are unverified beliefs and I found no source for them: per-hand simultaneous span at most 12-14 semitones (a 10th is about 15-16 semitones for large hands), at most 5 notes per hand, a cap on onsets per second, and a check that the left-hand accompaniment does not cross or overlap the melody register. | — | — | — | — | unverified belief | metric-definition

docs.title: Leads worth chasing
docs.text:
• Full text of Fang et al. 2020 ("Bach or Mock?") for its exact rule list, weights and any code (check the Pardo lab GitHub).
  • Whether the Coconet / Bach Doodle paper (arXiv 1907.06637) or the DeepBach/BachBot evaluations count parallel-5th/8ve rates, and how often Bach himself breaks them (a baseline rate).
  • Ramoneda et al. papers on fingering-based difficulty (e.g. "Score difficulty analysis for piano performance education based on fingering", ICASSP 2022) for a fingering-cost-as-difficulty formulation.
  • Nakamura's PIG code/model release (the fingering HMM binary) to check whether per-note fingering cost can be pulled out.
  • music21 theoryAnalyzer module (in alpha.theoryAnalysis) for batch counting of parallel fifths/octaves across a score; not checked this run.
  • A voice-separation algorithm for piano (e.g. Chew & Wu contig mapping, or music21's voiceLeading on chordify outer voices) to make the quartet checks usable on accompaniment texture.
  • incon model choice: compare hutch_78_roughness, har_18_harmonicity and har_19_composite on accompaniment chords.

docs.title: Looked for but not found
docs.text:
• A peer-reviewed automatic piano playability metric (hand span, per-hand polyphony, stretch) used to evaluate generated accompaniment. None turned up this run.
  • A music21 method for leading-tone or chordal-7th resolution, or for upper-voice spacing (more than an octave between S-A or A-T). Not present in the voiceLeading module docs I read; isProperResolution is interval-level only.
  • An evidence-backed recipe for applying 4-part voice-leading rules to free piano textures.
  • A Python, symbolic-input sensory-dissonance library other than incon (which is R).
  • Empirical correlation between rule-violation counts and human ratings of piano accompaniment specifically.

docs.title: D-variety-combination-r1-1: metrics for variety/creativity, their link to listening judgments, and how to combine them for best-of-N selection
docs.text: Decision served: choosing objective metrics to pick the best of 8 generated piano accompaniments (symbolic MIDI) and combining them into one selection rule. Accessed 2026-11-22. 14 tool calls. Only web sources were used; no project files were read.

docs.title: Metric definitions
docs.text:
• Pitch-class histogram entropy H = -sum_{i=0..11} h_i log2 h_i, where h is the normalised 12-bin pitch-class histogram. It is computed over 1 bar (H1) or 4 bars (H4). Lower means clearer tonality. Real jazz: H1=1.94, H4=2.87. Generated music: H1 2.17-2.45, H4 2.91-3.12. In other words, the generated music had HIGHER entropy than the real music, so maximising entropy is not "better". | Wu & Yang, "The Jazz Transformer on the Front Line", https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.01307 | ISMIR 2020 (peer-reviewed) | 2020 | accessed 2026-11-22 | high | metric-definition
  • Grooving pattern similarity GS(g^a, g^b) = 1 - (1/Q) sum_i XOR(g^a_i, g^b_i), where g is a binary vector marking the onset positions in a bar (Q=64), averaged over all pairs of bars. Higher means more consistent rhythm. Real = 0.86, models = 0.69-0.76. | same | ISMIR 2020 | 2020 | accessed 2026-11-22 | high | metric-definition
  • Chord progression irregularity CPI = % of unique chord trigrams in a piece. The paper does not state the exact denominator. Real = 40.4%, models = 72.6-81.2%. A second source warns that very low CPI can mean a boring progression. | same; Kader & Karmaker survey (below) | | | accessed 2026-11-22 | high (definition) / medium (denominator) | metric-definition
  • Structureness indicator SI_l^u = max over l<=i<=u, 1<=j<=N of S_ij, where S is the fitness scape plot (values in [0,1]) and N is the duration in seconds. It is reported at three timescales: SI(3-8), SI(8-15) and SI(15+). Real values are 0.35-0.36. Model values are 0.10-0.27, so the models fall short of the real music. | same | ISMIR 2020 | 2020 | accessed 2026-11-22 | high | metric-definition
  • Code: MusDr implements H, GS, CPI and SI: https://github.com/slSeanWU/MusDr | same | | | accessed 2026-11-22 | high | code-availability
  • MusPy metrics:
  • pitch_entropy: Shannon entropy of the normalised pitch histogram. Returns NaN if there are no notes.
  • pitch_class_entropy: the same entropy over a 12-bin pitch-class histogram.
  • polyphony: mean number of pitches sounding at once.
  • polyphony_rate: fraction of time steps where at least 2 pitches sound.
  • groove_consistency: mean Hamming distance between neighbouring measures. The docs give no explicit 1- normalisation, so check the code.
  • Also included: pitch_in_scale_rate, scale_consistency, empty_beat_rate, pitch_range, n_pitches_used.

| MusPy docs https://salu133445.github.io/muspy/doc/metrics.html ; Dong et al., "MusPy: A Toolkit for Symbolic Music Generation", https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.01951 | ISMIR 2020 (peer-reviewed) | 2020 | accessed 2026-11-22 | high | metric-definition / code-availability (https://github.com/salu133445/muspy) - Yang & Lerch, MGEval-style evaluation: they compute per-feature distributions of pitch/rhythm descriptors (pitch range, note count, pitch-class histogram, IOI, note-length histogram, etc.). They then compare generated and reference sets via KL divergence and overlapping area (OA) of the distributions, instead of maximising any feature. Their key finding is that models can misrepresent even low-level distributions such as pitch range and note count. | Yang & Lerch, "On the evaluation of generative models in music", https://musicinformatics.gatech.edu/wp-content_nondefault/uploads/2018/11/postprint.pdf | Neural Computing and Applications (peer-reviewed journal) | 2018 online / 2020 issue | accessed 2026-11-22 | high (approach) / medium (exact feature list, taken from survey excerpts, not the full text) | metric-definition / combination-method ("closeness to reference distribution") - Accompaniment-specific metrics: - Chord accuracy: generated harmony is checked against the given chord sequence. - Texture similarity: measured in the 256-D latent space of a pretrained texture VAE. - MUTE F1: computed at the 128-pitch level and at the pitch-class level.

Only search snippets were read, not the full texts. | Zhao et al., "Structured Multi-Track Accompaniment Arrangement via Style Prior Modelling", https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.16334 (NeurIPS 2023, unverified this run); "Emotion-Guided Music Accompaniment Generation Based on VAE", https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.04015 | | 2023 | accessed 2026-11-22 | medium | metric-definition

docs.title: Evidence on correlation with listening judgments
docs.text:
• No correlation computed in the Jazz Transformer paper. Its 59-listener study (27 "pros") rated the model below real pieces on every aspect (overall quality, impression, structureness, richness; one-tailed Z, p<0.05). The authors did NOT correlate the metrics with the ratings and left this as future work. The link is only suggestive. | Wu & Yang 2020 (above) | ISMIR 2020 | | accessed 2026-11-22 | high | empirical-correlation (negative evidence)
  • FMD, KLD and OA track listener rankings better than perplexity. For model-level ranking, FMD, KLD and OA "closely align with human judgments", while perplexity (PPL) diverges for the two largest models. No correlation coefficient is reported. There were only 5 raters, and the comparison is at model level, not per sample. A counter-example: Moonbeam has the highest OA (82.2%) but a mid-range subjective score (2.91 vs 3.22 for the best model). | Lehmkuhl et al., "Generating Piano Music with Transformers: A Comparative Study of Scale, Data, and Metrics", https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.07268 | AI for Music workshop / arXiv (not a full peer-reviewed venue) | v2 Jan 2026 | accessed 2026-11-22 | medium-low | empirical-correlation
  • The 2025 survey finds no symbolic correlation numbers. It reports poor metric-perception correlation in general, but cites no symbolic-specific correlation study. The only numbers it relies on are for audio metrics (Yuan et al. 2025: CLAP/FAD/KLD align poorly with human preference). It also says OA and KLD have no meaningful thresholds, and that a higher score does not guarantee better-sounding music. It proposes, but does not build, a learned quality scorer trained on preferences. | Kader & Karmaker, "A Survey on Evaluation Metrics for Music Generation", https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.00051 | arXiv preprint | Aug 2025 | accessed 2026-11-22 | medium | empirical-correlation
  • Another evaluation-methods survey. A 2025 survey says no general solution exists for evaluating generative music. | Lerch et al., "Survey on the Evaluation of Generative Models in Music", https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.05104 | arXiv (v4; venue not checked) | 2025 | accessed 2026-11-22 | medium | empirical-correlation (context)
  • Learned evaluators / reward models for symbolic music: none trained on human preferences over MIDI was found. The nearest are:
  • SMART renders MIDI to piano audio and uses Meta Audiobox Aesthetics "Content Enjoyment" as the reward. In a 14-listener study (399 observations), ratings rose by about 1.22 points (p=0.002).
  • NotaGen's CLaMP-DPO labels chosen/rejected samples by CLaMP 2 similarity to fine-tuning references, with no human labels. The exact formula was not retrieved.

| Jonason, Casini & Sturm, "SMART", https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.16839 (arXiv, Apr 2025); Wang et al., "NotaGen", https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.18008 (arXiv, Feb 2025) | preprints | 2025 | accessed 2026-11-22 | medium | empirical-correlation / code-availability (code URL for neither was confirmed)

docs.title: Combination methods and pitfalls
docs.text:
• Goodhart evidence: optimising one learned quality score caused collapse. In SMART, strong over-optimisation (1000 iterations, beta=0):
  • "dramatically reduces diversity of model outputs";
  • produced repeated patterns;
  • pushed note counts to about 70, empty-beat rate to 0, and widened pitch and velocity range;
  • gave scale consistency a heavier tail (more chromaticism);
  • made the reward score generated music ABOVE real piano recordings.

Lesson: a single maximised score drifts away from what real music looks like, so gate it or anchor it to a reference range. | SMART (above) | arXiv | 2025 | accessed 2026-11-22 | medium-high | combination-method (pitfall) - Target ranges instead of maximising, supported by the data. On H, CPI, GS and SI, real music is NOT at the extreme: entropy and CPI are lower in real music, GS and SI higher. A "closeness to the reference distribution" score (|x - mu_ref|/sd_ref, or OA/KLD as in Yang & Lerch) is therefore better supported than "maximise variety". | derived from Wu & Yang 2020 Table 2 + Yang & Lerch | | | accessed 2026-11-22 | medium (inference) | combination-method - Best-of-8 selection in a frontier system (YuE2), as described in a search snippet: 1. Pareto-dominance pruning across 3 metrics (Musicality, Q3O, PER). 2. Lexicographic tolerance windows: keep candidates within 0.10 of the best Musicality, then within 0.10 of the best remaining Q3O. 3. Pick the lowest PER.

The full text could not be parsed, so this is unverified beyond the snippet. | Yuan et al., "YuE2: Unifying Symbolic and Audio Music Generation at Frontier Quality", https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.33757 | arXiv | ~Sep 2026 | accessed 2026-11-22 | low-medium | combination-method - Rank aggregation instead of z-scores. One challenge paper ranks entries on each metric separately and sums the Borda ranks. This avoids putting different metric scales on a common footing, but it is coarse when N=8. | "Academic Text-to-Music Grand Challenge", https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.21538 | arXiv | 2026 | accessed 2026-11-22 | low-medium (snippet only) | combination-method - Weighted sum of normalised verifiers. SCORE (text-to-audio) normalises CLAP + Audiobox PQ and takes a weighted sum, warning against over-optimising a single verifier. | snippet from search https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.03589 / related; exact paper attribution unverified | arXiv | 2026 | accessed 2026-11-22 | low | combination-method

docs.title: Leads worth chasing
docs.text:
• Read the full text of YuE2's best-of-N section: dominance filter plus lexicographic tolerance. It is the closest published analogue to an "8 candidates, gate then maximise" rule.
  • Read Yang & Lerch's full text for the exact feature list and the OA/KLD procedure. Possibly use their MGEval code (github.com/RichardYang40148/mgeval; repo unverified this run).
  • Pearce's IDyOM, unverified belief: IC = -log2 p(event | context). Find studies that relate mean IC to ratings of interest or complexity (e.g. inverted-U preference). The search this run returned nothing relevant.
  • Syncopation measures (Longuet-Higgins & Lee; Witek et al. 2014, inverted-U between syncopation and groove/pleasure) could serve as a "creative within limits" target range. Unverified this run.
  • Zhao et al. 2023 and D3PIA (arXiv 2602.03523): check their definitions of chord-fidelity and texture-diversity metrics for accompaniment on POP909.
  • Check whether the NotaGen CLaMP 2 score could serve as a reference-similarity reranker for symbolic accompaniment, and find the code.

docs.title: Looked for but not found
docs.text:
• Per-sample correlation coefficients (r or rho) between symbolic feature metrics (entropy, GS, SI, polyphony) and listener ratings. No source this run reported any.
  • A reward model or learned evaluator trained on human preferences over symbolic music. Only audio-proxy (SMART) and reference-similarity (CLaMP-DPO) approaches were found.
  • Xiong et al. 2023, "A comprehensive survey for evaluation methodologies of AI-generated music", was not retrieved.
  • IDyOM information content as a creativity or interest predictor for generated music (search returned off-topic results).
  • Compression-based complexity metrics applied to generated accompaniment.
  • Music papers that explicitly compare z-score sums vs Pareto vs lexicographic rules for reranking.

docs.title: 技術​研究​：​配和聲​模型​與​和弦​條件​伴奏​生成
docs.text: ​這份​研究​服務​的​決定​： ​原型​ 02「​先定​和​聲​，​再生​伴奏​」​要​用​哪些​模型​和​資料​，​並把​結果​累積​進​ kb/。

docs.title: 執行​摘要
docs.text:
​建議​：​原型​ 02 ​拆成​兩段​分開​比​較​。​先比​「​誰​來​配和聲​」，​再​比​「​誰​來​把​和​聲彈​成​伴奏​」。 - ​配和聲​比三個​：MelodyT5、AccoMontage2、​語言​模型​。​用​你​親手配​的​和弦​當標準​答案​。 - ​伴奏​比三個​：AMT ​加上​和弦​條件​、AccoMontage、Polyffusion。 - ​每段​多生​幾份​，​用和聲​指標​挑​最好​的​。 - ​前提​是​和​聲要​正確​，​而​你​本身​就是​最​可靠​的​裁判​。

​推出​這個​建議​的​三個​發現​：

  1. 「​配和聲​」​和​「​吃​和弦​生​伴奏​」​都​有​開源​、MIT ​授權​、​有​權重​的​模型​，​而且​都​是​為​了​我們​這種​任務​設計​的​。​這是​前​一輪​沒查​到​的​。
  2. MelodyT5（ISMIR 2024）：​用​ ABC ​記譜​替​旋律​配​和弦​，​支援​七​和弦​和​轉位​。​程式​碼​和​ HF ​權重​都​是​ MIT，1.13 ​億參數​ [1][2]。
  3. AccoMontage2（ISMIR 2022）：​只給​旋律​，​就​能​同時​配和聲​、​生​伴奏​，​但​只​支援​ 4/4 ​拍​ [3][4]。
  4. AccoMontage、Polyffusion：​吃​「​旋律​＋​和弦​」​生鋼琴​伴奏​ [11][10]。
  5. ​這些​模型​多半​用​ POP909 ​訓練​，​它​是​「​旋律​＋​和弦​＋​鋼琴​伴奏​」​的​資料​集​ [21]。​原型​ 01 ​用​的​ AMT ​主要​學​的​是​流行歌​轉成​的​多樂器​ MIDI，​不是​為​「​單​旋律​配鋼琴​伴奏​」​設計​的​（R1 ​來源​ 10–12）。
  6. 「​和弦​正確​」​不​等​於​「​聽起​來和諧​」。 D3PIA ​的​聽覺​測試​發現​：​和弦​正確​率​最高​的​模型​（WSG，87.6%），​聽者​反而​覺得​比較​不和諧​，​因為​裡面​有​不協​和​的​音​ [8]。​所以​挑選​伴奏​時​，​要​同時​看​和弦​正確​率​、​調外音​比例​和​協和度​，​最後還​是​要​靠​耳朵​ [12]。​這呼​應前​一輪​的​發現​：​客觀​指標​和​聽者​評分​相關​很弱​（R1 ​來源​ 60）。
  7. ​讓​語言​模型​決定​和​聲​，​目前​沒有​嚴謹​證據​，​只有​零星​跡象​。
  8. ​沒有​任何​正式​評測​拿​一般​語言​模型​配和聲​，​和​專門​的​配和聲​模型​比較​ [20]。
  9. ​有利​的​跡象​：​用​文字​格式​（MIDI、LilyPond、MEI）​把​音符​餵給​語言​模型​時​，​和​聲​分析​的​表現​接近​滿分​或​不錯​ [15][16][17]。
  10. ​不利​的​跡象​：​遇到​半音​和​聲​多​的​曲子​就會​出錯​ [17]；​也​很​難​定位​到​特定​小節​ [18]，​這和前​一輪​ ABC-Eval ​的​發現​一致​（R1 ​來源​ 22）。
  11. ​原型​ 01 ​的​三段​旋律​都​是​自然​音階為​主​的​民謠​，​正好​是​語言​模型​表現​較​好​的​情況​。

​最大​的​限制​： ​東亞​、​中國​音樂​的​配和聲​資料​和​模型​都​沒​找到​。​附和​弦​標記​的​中國​民歌​語料​完全​沒有​；​最​接近​的​是​ OpenGufeng（​古風​流行​）​和​中國​合唱​資料​集​ [26][27]。​這和前​一輪​「​非西方​資料​稀少​」​的​結論​一致​（R1 D2）。​茉莉花​這類​旋律​，​現有​的​配和聲​模型​都​是​用​西方​資料​訓練​的​。

docs.title: 一​、​配和聲​模型​（​旋律​ → ​和弦​）
docs.text:
模型​ ​年份​／​會議​ ​授權​（​程式​碼​／​權重​） ​權重​ ​輸入​→​輸出​ ​訓練​資料​ Mac ​備​註​ MelodyT5 ISMIR 2024 MIT／MIT（HF ​標​籤​） ✅ HF ABC ​旋律​ → ​帶​和弦​記號​的​ ABC ​民謠​、​巴哈​聖詠​、Nottingham（​西方​） 1.13 ​億參數​，​應​可用​ CPU；​環境​寫​死​ Python 3.7、CUDA 11.6，​要​改​（​未驗證​） ​在​ 2 of 3 ​項​指標​上贏​ STHarm，​聽覺​測試​也​較​受​偏好​ [1][2] AccoMontage2 ISMIR 2022 MIT ​資料​檔​在​ Google Drive MIDI ​旋律​＋​主音​＋​樂句​切分​ → ​和弦​＋​伴奏​ Niko ​和弦​庫​（5,000＋​進行​）、POP909 README ​沒提​ GPU；​有​網頁​介面​ ​只​支援​ 4/4；​樂句​限​ 4 ​或​ 8 ​小節​；​四種​和弦​風格​ [3][4] ​單編​碼器​遮罩​式​配和聲​ arXiv 2026-01 Apache-2.0 ❌ ​音級​鋼琴卷​ → ​和​聲​ HookTheory ​未知​ ​摘要​說​幾乎​所有​指標​都贏​，​跨​領域​進步​最大​ [5] EMO_Harmonizer arXiv 2024 ​無​授權​ ✅ Google Drive ​事件​序列​ → MIDI HookTheory＋EMOPIA ​依賴​ CUDA ​專用​套件​，​可能​不行​ ​可以​依情緒​配和聲​ [6] STHarm／VTHarm IEEE Access 2022 ​無​授權​ ❌ ​要​自己​訓練​ — CMD、HookTheory ​假設​ CUDA ​附​ 9 ​種評​估指標​的​程式​ [7] B* ​限制​解碼​ AIMC 2025 ​論文​ CC BY 4.0 ？ ​旋律​＋​指定​和弦​ → ​和弦​ — ​搜尋​演算法​ ​可以​強制​某些​小節​用​你​指定​的​和弦​ [9]

​評估​的​標準​： Yeh ​等​人​（JNMR 2021）​比較​了​模板​比​對​、HMM、​基因​演算法​和​兩個​深度​模型​，​用​了​ 6 ​項​指標​和​ 202 ​位​聽者​，​是​這個​領域​常用​的​比​較​基準​ [13]。​常用​指標​有​ CTnCTR（​和弦音​比例​）、PCS（​音高​協和分數​）、MCTD（​旋律​與​和弦​的​調性​距離​）[1][13]。

​沒查​到​： music21 ​有​沒​有​現成​的​規則式​配和聲​工具​（​預算用​完​沒查​）；BART harmonization、MuPT、CoCoMulla。

docs.title: 二​、​吃​和弦​條件​的​伴奏​模型​（​旋律​＋​和弦​ → ​鋼琴​伴奏​）
docs.text:
模型​ ​年份​／​會議​ ​授權​ ​權重​ ​輸入​ ​訓練​資料​ Mac ​備​註​ AccoMontage ISMIR 2021 MIT ✅ Google Drive MIDI ​旋律​＋​和弦​（​以​拍​為​單位​，​可到​九​和弦​） POP909 ​樂句​庫​ ​檢索​＋​小型​ VAE，README ​沒提​ CUDA（​未驗證​） ​輸出​有​力度​和​踏板​，1–16 ​小節​樂句​ [11] Polyffusion ISMIR 2023 MIT ✅ SharePoint ​和弦​條件​、​織體​條件​、​旋律​補寫​ POP909 README ​沒​提裝置​ D3PIA ​測得​和弦​正確​率​ 37.5%，​調外音​ 0% [10][8] Compose & Embellish ICASSP 2023 MIT ✅ HF ​旋律​＋​和弦​（Embellish ​階段​） Pop1K7 ​建議​ CUDA 10.2 ​調外音​ 14.8%、​和弦​正確​率​ 58.1% [14][8] D3PIA ICASSP 2026 ​未知​ ❌ ​沒​找到​ ​旋律​＋​和弦​的​鋼琴卷​ POP909 ​只有​ 220 ​萬​參數​，8 ​小節​約​ 1.7 ​秒​ ​聽者​評分​最好​；​和弦​正確​率​ 80.1%，​調外音​ 0% [8] FGG ICML 2025（​依​ README） ​沒​看到​授權​ ✅ ​和弦​（​必要​）＋​旋律​ POP909 ​未驗證​ ​取樣​時​硬性​擋​掉​調外音​，​這個​技巧​可以​套用​到​其他​模型​ [19] Whole-Song Gen ICLR 2024 MIT ​部分​ ​曲式​＋​調​ POP909 ​慢​（GPU ​上​ 8 ​小節​ 79 ​秒​） ​和弦​正確​率​ 87.6%，​但​聽​起來​較​不和諧​ [8] AccoMontage-3 NeurIPS 2024 MIT ✅ ​旋律​＋​和弦​ → ​鋼琴​ → ​多軌​ LMD、Slakh2100 ​舊版​ PyTorch、Python ≤ 3.9 [24] GETMusic 2023 — README ​沒寫​ ​多軌​ ​未公開​ — ​所屬​的​ muzic repo ​已​於​ 2026-10-01 ​封存​ [25]

「​多生​幾份​挑​最好​的​」： ​沒有​找到​任何​論文​對​鋼琴​伴奏​這樣​做​ [12]。​最​接近​的​是​ 2026 ​年​一篇​檢索式​論文​：​用​一個​綜合​分數​（​和​聲​吻合​、​聲部​進行​、​風格​、​重​複​度​）​挑選​ POP909 ​的​伴奏​樂句​，​但​沒​有​程式​碼​，​也​沒​有​聽覺​測試​ [23]。​這是​一個​可以​自己​做​的​空白​。

​可以​拿來​挑選​的​指標​： ​和弦​正確​率​、​調外音​比例​（OOK）、​和弦​嵌入​相似​度​、​和弦音​比例​（CTnCTR）、​音高​協和分數​（PCS）、​旋律​與​伴奏​的​協​和​／​不協​和​重疊​比例​ [12]。

docs.title: 三​、​語言​模型​配和聲​的​證據
docs.text:
研究​ ​模型​ ​發現​ ​可信度​ Carone ​等​人​（PMLR 2026） Gemini 2.5 Pro／Flash、Qwen2.5-Omni ​用​ MIDI ​文字​輸入​時​，​和弦​性質​辨識​接近​滿分​；​改成​音訊​就​大幅​下降​。​提示​技巧​幫助​不大​ [15] ​中​（​只讀​摘要​） Pond ​與​ Fujinaga（CSME 2025） ChatGPT、Claude、Gemini ​樂理​考試​：​用​ MEI ​格式​最好​，Claude ​加上​情境​教學達​ 75%；​和弦​分析​的​進步​最少​ [16] ​中​ Augmented Fifth ​部落​格​（2026-08） Claude Opus 5、Gemini 3.1 Pro、Grok 4.5 ​羅​馬​數字​分析​：​巴哈​、​蕭邦表現​不錯​，​史​克里​亞賓​全部​出錯​（​漏掉​掛留音​、​副屬​和弦​）；​用​ LilyPond ​文字​可以​，​用樂譜​圖片​不行​ [17] ​低​（​只有​ 3 ​段​、​單一評​分者​） MSU-Bench（ACL 2026） 15 ​個​以上​模型​ ​很難​定位​到​特定​小節​，​連帶​影響​和​聲題​ [18] ​中​ ComposerX（2024） GPT-4 ​多​代理人​ ​有​一個​「​和​聲​代理人​」​負責加​和弦​，​並檢查​和弦​與​旋律​的​調性​是否​相符​，​是​最​接近​「​語言​模型​指揮​」​的​設計​ [19b] ​低中​

​解讀​： 「​語言​模型​先寫​和弦​、​程式​負責​檢查​和​執行​」​這個​混合​設計​有​前例​，​例如​ Carone ​等​人用​的​ LogicLM ​作法​ [15]、ComposerX [19b]、Libretto [20b]。​但​沒​有人​量過​它​配出​來​的​和​聲​好不好​。​這​正好​可以​在​原型​ 02 ​裡​，​用​你​配​的​和弦​當標準​答案​來量​。

docs.title: 四​、​附和​弦​標記​的​旋律​資料​（​新增​到​資料​目錄​）
docs.text:
資料​集​ ​規模​ ​內容​ ​授權​ ​風格​ POP909 909 ​首​ ​旋律​＋​副​旋律​＋​鋼琴​伴奏​＋​和弦​／​調​／​拍​（​演算法​標記​） MIT（repo ​標​籤​） ​流行​（​是否​為華語​未​在​本輪​確認​）[21] Hooktheory ​約​ 50 ​小時​ ​旋律​＋​和​聲​標記​ CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 ​西方​流行​ [22] Chordonomicon ​約​ 68 ​萬條​和弦​進行​ ​只有​和弦​，​沒有​旋律​ CC BY-NC 4.0 ​西方​流行​／​搖滾​ [28] When-in-Rome ​約​ 2,000 ​份羅馬​數字​分析​ ​含​ 371 ​首​巴哈​聖詠​、​貝多芬​四重奏​等​ ​新內容​ CC BY-SA 4.0 ​西方​古典​ [29] Chord Melody Dataset ​少​於​ 650 ​首​ ​爵士​標準​曲​旋律​＋​和弦​ MIT（​但​原曲​可能​有版權​） ​爵士​ [30] OpenGufeng ​未標示​ ​旋律​＋​三​和弦​ MIT ​中國風​流行​ [26] ​中國​合唱​資料​集​ 125 ​首​、441 ​段​ ​含​和弦​標記​ ​未讀​ ​中國​合唱​ [27] Essen ​中國​民歌​調式​標記​ 219 ​首​ ​調式​標記​（​不是​和弦​） CC BY 4.0，​限制​存取​ ​中國​民歌​ [31] MelodyHub 26.19 ​萬首​ ABC ​配和聲​是​七種​任務​之一​ ​未讀​ ​民謠​、​西方​為主​ [1]

​沒查證​： Wikifonia、Nottingham、McGill Billboard、Rock Corpus、DCML。

docs.title: 跨​面向​洞察
docs.text:
• ​我們​做​的​任務​，​正好​是​ POP909 ​這​一支​研究​在​做​的​。 「​旋律​＋​和弦​ → ​鋼琴​伴奏​」​是​ POP909 ​系列​模型​的​標準​任務​（AccoMontage、Polyffusion、D3PIA、FGG），AMT ​不是​。​原型​ 01 ​的​伴奏​不好​，​很​可能​是​選錯​了​工具​，​而​不​只是​少​了​和​聲​控制​。​不過​這些​模型​學​的​都​是​流行歌​，​配​古典​或民謠​旋律​時​，​風格​可能​會​不​對​（​推論​）。
  • ​評估​方法​又​一次​成為​空白​。 「​多生​幾份​挑​最好​的​」​沒​有人​做過​；「​和弦​正確​」​和​「​聽起​來和諧​」​又​會​分歧​。​這呼​應前​一輪​的​洞察​：​評估​方法​本身​就​可以​是​研究​貢獻​（R1 ​跨​面向​洞察​）。​你​擅長​心理​計量​和​聽覺​實驗​，​正好​派​得​上​用場​。
  • ​非西方​資料​仍​是​最大​缺口​。 ​配和聲​、​伴奏​兩邊​都​沒​有用​中國​或​東亞​語料​訓練​的​模型​。​這和前​一輪​的​ D2、D3 ​一致​：​跨文化​這條​路​必須​從​自己​整理​資料​開始​。

docs.title: 建議
docs.text:
1. ​原型​ 02 ​的​配和聲​段​：​比較​三種​配和聲​方法​，​用​你​配​的​和弦​當標準​答案​。 ​信心​：​中​高​。
  2. ​三種​方法​：MelodyT5、AccoMontage2、​語言​模型​。
  3. ​你​替​三段​旋律​親手配​一份​和弦​，​量​每個​方法​和​標準​答案​的​一致​程度​。
  4. ​這​正好​回應​你​說​的​前提​「​和​聲標​記要​正確​」。
  5. ​注意​：AccoMontage2 ​只​支援​ 4/4，​綠​袖子​（3/4）​不能​用​；​茉莉花​（2/4）​可以​兩小節​併​成​一小​節​。
  6. ​對應​原型​ 02 ​計畫​的​〈​要​比​較​的​選項​〉。
  7. ​伴奏​段​：​比較​三種​生​伴奏​方法​，​和弦​都​用​同​一份​。 ​信心​：​中​。
  8. ​三種​方法​：AMT ​加上​和弦​條件​、AccoMontage、Polyffusion。
  9. AMT ​是​現成​流程​，​加上​和弦​條件​的​改動​最小​；​另外​兩個​是​為​這個​任務​設計​的​ MIT ​模型​。
  10. ​它們​在​ Mac ​上能​不能​跑​，​只​看​了​ README，​要​先​做​簡單​的​試​跑​。
  11. D3PIA ​評價​最好​，​但​找​不到​程式​碼​，​先記​在​知識​庫裡​，​持續​觀察​。
  12. ​每種​組合生​ 8 ​份​，​用和聲​指標​挑​最好​的​，​最後用​耳朵​確認​。 ​信心​：​中​。​指標​用​ CTnCTR、PCS、​調外音​比例​，​加上​旋律​與​伴奏​的​不協​和​重疊​比例​。D3PIA ​的​研究​顯示​，​單看​和弦​正確​率會​挑錯​ [8]。
  13. ​知識庫​： ​這一輪​新增​的​模型​、​資料​集​、​文獻​都​已​經放進​ kb/。POP909 ​和​ When-in-Rome ​是​之​後​自己​訓練​時​最​值得​先​拿到​的​兩個​資料​集​（​授權​寬​鬆​、​標記​完整​）。
  14. ​暫不微調​，​這是​你​已經​做​的​決定​。​之後要​做​跨文化​，​需要​自己​整理​附和​弦​標記​的​中國​民歌​資料​。

docs.title: 待解​問題
docs.text:
• MelodyT5、AccoMontage、Polyffusion ​在​ Mac ​上​跑​不​跑​得動​：​要​實際試​跑​。
  • D3PIA ​的​程式​碼​到底​有​沒​有​公開​：​專案​頁​沒​有​連結​。
  • FGG ​的​授權​：README ​沒有​授權​檔​。
  • POP909 ​的​曲目​是不是​華語​流行​：​本輪​沒​確認​。
  • music21 ​有​沒​有​規則式​的​配和聲​工具​，​可以​當最​簡單​的​基準​：​本輪​沒查​。
  • ​語言​模型​配和聲​的​品質​：​沒有​正式​評測​，​原型​ 02 ​會​自己​量​。
