LICENSE.md and DISCLAIMER.md exist but were not read. The HF dataset API returned an auth error) | dataset licence. Paper: OpenReview (https://openreview.net/pdf?id=X5hrhgndxW). OpenAI is pending before the Munich Court of Appeals" and the judgment "remains under appeal" | Reed Smith blog, "GEMA notches a second transatlantic AI copyright win in Germany" | https://www.reedsmith.com/our-insights/blogs/viewpoints/102nfis/gema-notches-a-second-transatlantic-ai-copyright-win-in-germany/ | Reed Smith (law firm) | 2026-07 | accessed 2026-11-19 | medium (one law-firm source for the appeal status. docs.title: Leads
docs.text:
• Conflict: YourMT3 code is GPL-3.0 (GitHub) but the checkpoints are Apache-2.0 (HF). Check whether the HF Space code is also GPL, and what licences the training data (Slakh, MusicNet, and others) carry.
  • Provenance risk: AMT weights are Apache-2.0 but were trained on "450k commercial music records". ACE-Step 1.5 training data is undisclosed or unchecked. After GEMA v Suno ("the model itself infringes"), a permissive weights licence does not equal commercial safety in the EU. Next: read the ACE-Step 1.5 tech report's data section.
  • Get a second source for GEMA v Suno (31 Jul 2026), for example the GEMA press release or juris/beck-aktuell. Also find out whether Suno appealed, and the OLG München docket or hearing date for OpenAI.
  • Read the Aria-MIDI DISCLAIMER.md and LICENSE.md. Read the Llama 3.2 licence clauses that apply to MIDI-LLM.
  • Check the PDMX.csv licence column: are any songs CC-BY (needing attribution) rather than PD or CC0 inside no_license_conflict?
  • Find the US Copyright Office generative AI training report (Part 3, May 2025 pre-publication) and whether a final version has been issued. Not covered this round.

docs.title: Looked for, not found
docs.text:
• An official ACE-Step statement that the weights are licensed differently from the MIT code: none found. The repo README and both HF cards say MIT.
  • Any OLG München appellate decision or hearing in GEMA v OpenAI as of 2026-11: none found.
  • Any 2026 settlement or judgment in Sony v Udio or UMG/Sony v Suno (US): none found in one search.
  • CompMusic jingju access restrictions: the Zenodo records found are all "open". A restricted "Jingju a cappella part1" or a restricted audio collection was not located, so this claim is not evidenced.
  • A second independent source for the MAESTRO, Saraga and M4Singer licences: not fetched, because the budget ran out. Each rests on the official page alone.
  • The US Copyright Office training report: not searched, because the budget ran out.

docs.title: D2 Datasets & Licensing — Round 1, digest 1
docs.text: Scope: Q1–Q5 of D2 (symbolic/performance data, paired score–audio, singing with scores, non-Western data, licensing reality). Budget used: 15 tool calls. Pages read directly: about 6 primary pages (MAESTRO page, PDMX Zenodo v9, arXiv 2601.00299 abstract page, Lakh MIDI project page, ASAP GitHub README), plus search snippets that quote primary records. Where a claim rests on a search-engine summary instead of a page I read myself, confidence is downgraded and the claim is marked "(via search snippet)".

docs.text: Format: claim | source title | URL | publisher | pub_date | accessed | confidence | class | peer-review

docs.text:
• MAESTRO v3.0.0: 198.7 h, 1,276 performances, paired MIDI+WAV from the Piano-e-Competition (Disklavier). MIDI includes velocity and pedals. About 3 ms note–audio alignment.   • Lakh MIDI: LMD-full has 176,581 de-duplicated MIDI files; LMD-matched/aligned have 45,129 files matched or aligned to Million Song Dataset 7digital previews. The audio previews are not distributed. That last point is my inference, not stated on the page. | same | same | Colin Raffel | live | 2026-11-19 | high (licence string) / medium (inference) | licence
  • PDMX v9 (2025-06): over 250K MusicXML scores scraped from MuseScore and filtered to Public Domain Mark or CC0. The record licence is CC BY 4.0. docs.title: Q2 Paired score + performance/audio
docs.text:
• ASAP: 222 MusicXML/MIDI scores aligned with 1,067–1,068 MIDI performances (over 92 h) of Western classical piano. Annotations cover beats, downbeats, time signatures and keys. 519 performances have audio, which must be pulled from MAESTRO v2.0.0. Licence CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. The README's own counts are inconsistent (222 vs 236 scores; 1,067 vs 1,068 performances). | ASAP dataset README | https://github.com/fosfrancesco/asap-dataset | F. Foscarin et al. (GitHub) | live | 2026-11-19 | high | dataset-size, licence
  • MAESTRO (above) is the main audio↔performance-MIDI pair. ASAP adds the score layer on top of MAESTRO. Both are NC-SA, so any score→performance→audio pipeline trained on them inherits non-commercial terms (inference).

docs.title: Q3 Singing voice with score alignment
docs.text:
• M4Singer: multi-style, multi-singer Mandarin singing with manually labelled alignment and musical scores. The paper states it is "noncommercially used under license CC BY-NC-SA 4.0". The licence is reported as CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, but only by a Hugging Face README; one derivative is tagged GPL-2.0, which conflicts. ACE-Opencpop (about 130 h re-curation) is reported as CC BY-NC 4.0. | HF READMEs | https://huggingface.co/datasets/255doesnotexist/GreendamOpencpop | Hugging Face (third party) | n/a | 2026-11-19 | low | licence

  • Gezi Opera (​歌仔​戲​) audio–text alignment dataset, built to train the FT-GAN singing-voice synthesis model. Licence and size were not found. | FT-GAN project page | https://zhengmidon.github.io/FTGAN.github.io/ | project page | n/a | 2026-11-19 | low | availability

docs.title: Q4 Non-Western / traditional
docs.text:
• Jingju Music Scores Collection v2.0 (2018): metadata and annotations are CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, and the Zenodo record is listed as restricted (login/request needed). ND blocks redistributing modified versions. | Zenodo jingju scores | https://zenodo.org/record/1245942 or https://zenodo.org/record/1286350 (search result; exact record for the scores collection not confirmed) | Zenodo / MTG-UPF | 2018 | 2026-11-19 | medium (via search snippet) | licence, availability
  • Taiwanese opera (Kua-á-hì / ​歌仔​戲​): a vocal-segment + lyrics dataset built from archival TV episodes, using OCR of burned-in subtitles plus speech/music activity detection. Size is not stated. No tune (​曲調​) labels; tune retrieval is mentioned only as a possible downstream task. The code is public (z-huang/ocr-subtitle-editor); dataset release is not stated. The CC BY 4.0 shown on arXiv covers the paper, not the data. Venue is ISMIR 2025 Late-Breaking Demo, which is not a full peer-reviewed paper. Authors include Li Su (Academia Sinica). | Timed text extraction from Taiwanese Kua-á-hì TV series (arXiv 2601.00299) | https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.00299v1 | arXiv | 2026-01 | 2026-11-19 | high (that it exists) / low (on access) | dataset, availability | ISMIR 2025 LBD
  • SymbTr (Turkish makam): repo licence CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Versions range from about 2,200 pieces / 155 makams (older) to about 3,000 pieces / 164 makams (v2.4.x). Formats are txt/MusicXML/MIDI/PDF. The latest release is on GitHub. | MTG/SymbTr GitHub; Zenodo SymbTr v2.4.3 | https://github.com/MTG/symbtr ; https://zenodo.org/records/160552 | MTG-UPF | 2016 | 2026-11-19 | medium (via search snippet; LICENSE file not opened) | licence, dataset-size | ISMIR 2012 paper (peer-reviewed)
  • Saraga (Carnatic + Hindustani, audio with annotations; v1.5 on Zenodo): the collections are described as "shared under Creative Commons licenses", but the exact licence on the data was not confirmed. The EMR 2021 paper is CC BY-NC 4.0, and the Zenodo 1.0 record asks users to email about their research. | Saraga Zenodo / UPF repository | https://zenodo.org/records/4301737 ; https://repositori.upf.edu/items/d4721c01-e38d-490b-b2d1-889f6dcd211d | MTG-UPF | 2018 / 2021 | 2026-11-19 | low | licence | Empirical Musicology Review 2021 (peer-reviewed)
  • Pattern across sources (synthesis): CompMusic non-Western corpora (jingju, makam, Indian) are consistently NonCommercial, sometimes NoDerivatives or restricted-access, and mostly audio + annotations. Large symbolic corpora exist only for makam (SymbTr) and jingju scores. This is a pattern seen across the rows above, not a single-source claim.

docs.title: Q5 Licensing reality / legal developments
docs.text:
• GEMA v OpenAI, Munich Regional Court I, 11 Nov 2025 (42 O 14139/24): the court held that memorising lyrics in model weights and reproducing them in outputs infringes copyright. The TDM exception does not cover storing or outputting protected lyrics, and OpenAI's claim to research-organisation privilege was rejected. The judgment covers 9 songs, is not final, and is likely appealed. GEMA also has separate proceedings against Suno. | Taylor Wessing, Bird & Bird, GEMA notices | https://www.taylorwessing.com/de/insights-and-events/insights/2025/11/gema-v-openai ; https://cm.twobirds.com/en/insights/2025/landmark-ruling-of-the-munich-regional-court-(gema-v-openai)-on-copyright-and-ai-training ; https://www.gema.de/en/w/landmark-ruling-gema-against-openai | law firms + GEMA (independent publishers) | 2025-11 | 2026-11-19 | medium (via search snippets from several independent publishers; the current appeal status in Nov 2026 is NOT checked, so this is over 12 months old) | legal
  • Implication for this project (inference): the main risks are memorisation and reproduction of protected material, not training as such. Corpora built from copyrighted repertoire carry risk if a model regurgitates them in stimuli (Lakh = pop transcriptions, Aria-MIDI/GiantMIDI = YouTube-derived performances). PDMX no_license_conflict is the cleanest large symbolic corpus. NC licences (MAESTRO, ASAP, Aria-MIDI, SymbTr, jingju, M4Singer) suit academic research-stimulus use but block commercial reuse of the trained model or outputs, depending on how "derivative" is read. That last point is legally unsettled.

docs.title: Leads
docs.text:
1. Contradictions to resolve: Opencpop licence (CC BY-NC-ND vs GPL-2.0 tag) needs a check against the official repo. The ASAP README's internal counts disagree. The Aria-MIDI licence is "other" on one mirror and CC BY-NC-SA on the HF card.
  2. Two-source rule still unmet for most licence claims. Open the live LICENSE/record pages for: SymbTr LICENSE, Saraga Zenodo 1.5 licence field, jingju scores record, POP909 repo, Aria-MIDI HF card, GiantMIDI disclaimer.md.
  3. Taiwanese opera: contact or follow up with Li Su's lab (Academia Sinica MCT Lab) on the Kua-á-hì dataset release. The FT-GAN Gezi Opera dataset needs its access terms found. Also check Taiwan's National Center for Traditional Arts (​國立​傳統​藝術​中心​) and the Taiwan Music Institute for archive access.
  4. GEMA v OpenAI appeal status (2026). GEMA v Suno outcome. Suno/Udio–major label settlements and licensing deals (2025). US Copyright Office Part 3 report on generative-AI training. EU AI Act GPAI training-data summary obligations (applying from Aug 2025). None of these were checked this run.
  5. Newer large symbolic sets from 2025–2026 (for example any successors to Aria-MIDI or PDMX, MidiCaps, GigaMIDI). Not searched this run.
  6. Aria-MIDI size: my belief is about 1M+ MIDI files / about 100k h. This is unverified and needs a fetch of the paper.

docs.title: Looked for, not found
docs.text:
• A dataset-level licence for POP909, and an ASAP-independent licence for the ASAP audio portion (it inherits MAESTRO's).
  • A downloadable Taiwanese opera (​歌仔​戲​) dataset with stated licence or access terms. Neither the Kua-á-hì paper nor the FT-GAN page gives one.

  • Japanese traditional music, Arab-Andalusian (CompMusic/Dunya) and minority/indigenous archives: not searched, out of budget. No claims are made about them.

docs.title: D3: Representing music beyond 12-TET (round 1, digest 1)
docs.text: Accessed 2026-11-19. Budget used: 14 search/fetch calls. Most claims rest on search-result snippets and abstract pages, not on full papers. Confidence is set to match.

docs.title: Findings
docs.text: Format: claim | source title | URL | publisher | pub_date | accessed | confidence | class | peer-review status

docs.title: Q1. Limits of MIDI and staff notation, and how current standards handle them
docs.text:
• MIDI 2.0 carries per-note pitch through Note On attributes and per-note pitch controllers. Pitch Bend is 32-bit, so microtonal per-note pitch is possible at spec level. Under default MIDI 1.0 to 2.0 translation the attribute type is "none" unless a MIDI-CI Profile sets it. | The state of MIDI 2.0: high-resolution performance and the rise of profiles (update Feb 2026) / midi.org quick reference | https://midi.org/the-state-of-midi-2-0-high-resolution-performance-and-the-rise-of-profiles-update-feb-2026 ; https://midi.org/?p=6489 | MIDI Association | 2026-02 | accessed 2026-11-19 | medium (seen through search snippets; spec PDF not read) | capability | standards body
  • The "7.9 fixed-point pitch" format of the per-note pitch attribute (7-bit semitone plus 9-bit fraction, about 0.2 cent) is reported only by forum users. I did not check it against the spec. Users also found no confirmed list of synths or players that honour arbitrary per-note pitch, so real implementation support is unproven. | Are there more than 128 notes in MIDI 2.0? | https://www.kvraudio.com/forum/viewtopic.php?p=8160672 | KVR Audio forum | n/a | accessed 2026-11-19 | low | availability | forum, not authoritative
  • MusicXML handles quarter tones natively: accidental values quarter-flat/sharp and three-quarters-flat/sharp, plus a numeric decimal <alter> (e.g. 0.5). Finer divisions such as 1/12-tone and HEJI go through SMuFL glyph attributes (supported "as of MusicXML 3.1"). The accidental names do not define exact tunings. | W3C public-music-notation-contrib posts (M. Good 2016; 2020 thread) | https://lists.w3.org/Archives/Public/public-music-notation-contrib/2016Jul/0007.html ; https://lists.w3.org/Archives/Public/public-music-notation-contrib/2020May/0008.html | W3C Music Notation CG | 2016-07 / 2020-05 | accessed 2026-11-19 | medium | capability | mailing list of spec maintainers
  • In practice MusicXML round-trips lose microtonal accidentals. Dorico reads them but does not export them, and OpenMusic 8 import ignores them. | Microtonality and MusicXML; IRCAM forum thread | https://forums.steinberg.net/t/microtonality-and-musicxml/863784 ; https://discussion.forum.ircam.fr/t/musicxml-import-still-ignores-quarter-tone-accidentals-in-openmusic-8-0/183126 | Steinberg / IRCAM forums | n/a | accessed 2026-11-19 | low-medium | availability | forum
  • MEI separates the written accidental (@accid) from the sounding one (@accid.ges). Quarter-tone values (qf, qs) exist. I found no cents-valued attribute. | MEI Guidelines v5, accid; MEI-L "Encoding quarter tones" | https://music-encoding.org/guidelines/v5/elements/accid.html ; https://lists.uni-paderborn.de/pipermail/mei-l/2016/001858.html | Music Encoding Initiative | v5 / 2016 | accessed 2026-11-19 | medium | capability | standards docs
  • Conceptual limit: the VocalNotes project asks whether the "note" (onset, duration, pitch) is the right unit for many traditions. It also asks whether ornaments are separate notes or part of the note they decorate. This bears directly on glides, ornaments and heterophony. | VocalNotes (IFTAWM journal) | https://journal.iftawm.org/?p=4218 | IFTAWM journal | unknown | accessed 2026-11-19 | low (snippet only) | method | journal; peer-review status unverified

docs.title: Q2. Symbolic representations for non-Western music in ML
docs.text:
• SymbTr (Turkish makam): about 3,000 pieces, 164 makams and roughly 1.2M notes in v3.0, released as text, MusicXML, PDF, MIDI and mu2. Licence is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, which blocks commercial use. Older releases have about 2,200 pieces and 155 makams (Karaosmanoğlu, ISMIR 2012). A phrase dataset adds 31,362 expert-annotated phrases over 480 scores. | SymbTr on Zenodo / GitHub MTG/symbtr | https://zenodo.org/records/15470412 ; https://github.com/MTG/symbtr | UPF-MTG (CompMusic) | 2016-10 (v3 record) | accessed 2026-11-19 | medium (licence comes from a snippet; live licence page not read; one source) | dataset-size, licence | ISMIR 2012 paper, peer-reviewed
  • Gongche (​工尺​譜​) OMR: Chen and Sheu (2014) built an OMR system for handwritten Kunqu gongche scores and evaluated it on only 39 images. A 2021 deep-learning follow-up and a 2024 algorithm comparison exist. A 2024 chapter says Chinese traditional-music OMR "is still limited". I found no public gongche OMR dataset. | An optical music recognition system for traditional Chinese Kunqu Opera scores written in Gong-Che notation | https://asmp-eurasipjournals.springeropen.com/articles/10.1186/1687-4722-2014-7 ; https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-031-70552-6_3 | EURASIP J. Audio Speech Music Proc.; Springer | 2014; 2024 | accessed 2026-11-19 | medium | dataset-size, availability | peer-reviewed (EURASIP JASMP 2014)
  • Suzipu/banzipu (Song-dynasty notation, KuiSCIMA): Repolusk and Veas released a public dataset. Search snippets name it as the exception among East-Asian OMR work. | Proceedings of the 6th International Workshop on Reading Music Systems | https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.15741 | WoRMS | 2024-11 | accessed 2026-11-19 | medium | dataset | workshop proceedings
  • Jianpu (​簡譜​) OMR: large annotated jianpu-plus-lyrics datasets are rare. Earlier attempts used synthetic or rendered scores. A Dec 2025 pipeline uses mostly classical computer vision ("expert systems") so it needs no large training set. Other work: an MDPI multi-font CNN dataset (Electronics 11(21):3592, 2022) and Wu (2017, IJMDEM). | The Renaissance of Expert Systems: Optical Recognition of Printed Chinese Jianpu Musical Scores with Lyrics | https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.14758v1 | arXiv | 2025-12 | accessed 2026-11-19 | medium | availability | preprint
  • Jingju scores: the Jingju Music Scores Collection has 92 machine-readable scores covering 897 melodic lines. These are Western-staff transcriptions, which is a fact about the corpus and not a claim that staff suffices. | Annotated jingju arias / CompMusic jingju resources | https://compmusic.upf.edu/zh-hans/node/349 | UPF-MTG | ~2017 | accessed 2026-11-19 | medium | dataset-size | dataset page

docs.title: Q3. MIR on Chinese opera (jingju, Gezaixi)
docs.text:
• The jingju a cappella singing dataset (ISMIR 2017) covers 120 arias and 1,265 melodic lines and is openly available. A related ground-truth release (Gong, Yang and Serra, SMC 2016) provides pYIN f0 tracks, note transcriptions and segmentation. Audio is held back for size and available on request. Jingju MIR therefore pairs continuous f0 with note-level annotation, as in a hybrid. | Jingju a cappella singing dataset (ISMIR 2017); Zenodo pitch-contour segmentation ground truth | https://archives.ismir.net/ismir2017/paper/000119.pdf ; https://zenodo.org/records/832736 | ISMIR / UPF | 2017-07 | accessed 2026-11-19 | medium-high | dataset-size, method | peer-reviewed (ISMIR 2017; SMC 2016)
  • Gezaixi/Kua-á-hì: the only MIR work I found builds vocal segments plus lyrics from archival TV. It separates singing from speech by OCR subtitle display duration and targets lyrics identification and tune (​曲調​) retrieval. It provides no pitch or score representation, and no dataset size is stated. Code is at z-huang/ocr-subtitle-editor. Release of the dataset itself is not stated. | Timed text extraction from Taiwanese Kua-á-hì TV series (Huang, Tsai, Hung, Wu, Wei, Su) | https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.00299v1 | arXiv (ISMIR 2025 LBD) | 2026-01 | accessed 2026-11-19 | high (for what it states) | dataset, availability | late-breaking demo, not full peer review
  • Further jingju MIR exists, for example arXiv 1708.03986 and Yukun Li's QMUL PhD thesis on jingju singing. I did not read them. | — | https://pdf.arxiv.org/pdf/1708.03986 ; https://webspace.eecs.qmul.ac.uk/s.e.dixon/phd/YukunLi-PhD-Thesis.pdf | — | — | accessed 2026-11-19 | low | lead | unread

docs.title: Q4. Continuous pitch vs discrete notes in computational ethnomusicology
docs.text:
• Tzanetakis (ICMC-SMC 2014) frames computational ethnomusicology as part of MIR. He notes that pitch discretisation is a cultural or instrument convention. Earlier systems (ISMIR 2006, Tarsos) start from continuous pitch and avoid a priori pitch categories. | Computational ethnomusicology (ICMC-SMC 2014) | https://speech.di.uoa.gr/ICMC-SMC-2014/images/VOL_1/0069.pdf | ICMC-SMC | 2014 | accessed 2026-11-19 | medium (snippet) | method | peer-reviewed conference; historical
  • Learned discrete contour tokens are an emerging hybrid. A VQ-VAE tokenises pitch-contour segments of Korean sigimsae ornaments into a learned vocabulary. The authors argue predefined note or ornament categories depend on manual labour. | Pitch Contour Tokenization using VQ-VAE and Its Application on Korean Traditional Music Analysis | https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.10979 | arXiv | 2026-08 | accessed 2026-11-19 | medium (snippet) | method | preprint
  • Stabilised-pitch-contour distributions beat note-level features for classifying Ethiopian Orthodox chant modes (silt). | arXiv 2412.18788 | https://arxiv.org/pdf/2412.18788 | arXiv | 2024-12 | accessed 2026-11-19 | low (snippet, single source) | benchmark | preprint
  • Oral-tradition tunings can be derived from f0 histograms aligned to MIDI by DTW. | arXiv 2503.11956 | https://www.arxiv.org/pdf/2503.11956 | arXiv | 2025-03 | accessed 2026-11-19 | low | method | preprint

docs.title: Q5. Generative models for non-12-TET music
docs.text:
• GaMaDHaNi (Hindustani vocal) is a two-level hierarchy: a generator over a finely quantised pitch contour feeds a contour-to-audio synthesiser conditioned on singer. The contour is modelled both as discrete tokens (autoregressive transformer) and as continuous values (diffusion). It produces a mel-spectrogram, then audio via Griffin-Lim. The authors explicitly reject "coarse discrete symbols" for melody and argue the contour layer enables primed generation and coarse pitch conditioning for human-AI interaction. Paper licence is CC BY 4.0; no code link appears on the abstract page. | Hierarchical Generative Modeling of Melodic Vocal Contours in Hindustani Classical Music (Shikarpur et al.) | https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.12658v2 | ISMIR 2024 | 2024-08 | accessed 2026-11-19 | high (architecture); historical (over 6 months old) | method, capability | peer-reviewed (ISMIR 2024)
  • A follow-up human-AI interaction study with Hindustani musicians uses the same system. | Exploratory Study of Human-AI Interaction for Hindustani Music | https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.13846 | arXiv | 2024-11 | accessed 2026-11-19 | low (unread) | lead | preprint (status unverified)

docs.title: Leads
docs.text:
1. Contradiction or tension: MIDI 2.0 can express per-note microtonal pitch on paper, but no implementer list confirms it works in practice. Next, read the official UMP spec (M2-104) and the MIDI Association "Note On pitch 7.9" profile, and check MPE (MIDI 1.0 per-channel bend) support in synths and DAWs.
  2. GaMaDHaNi's contour-as-intermediate design is the clearest template for a "score layer to performance layer" split in contour-centric traditions. Check whether code and data have been released, and whether it has been ported to Carnatic, jingju or Gezaixi.
  3. Find Carnatic gamaka-specific representations: the "compact gamaka representation" and "non-uniform pitch quantisation preserving raga characteristics" papers cited by GaMaDHaNi.
  4. Read the VQ-VAE contour tokenisation paper (2608.10979) in full as a candidate tokeniser for ​歌仔​戲​ and jingju glides. It is a preprint.
  5. Look for jingju or Kunqu generative models and singing-voice synthesis. Also look for Chinese opera SVS datasets such as Opencpop-style corpora for ​戲曲​.
  6. Check whether the Kua-á-hì dataset will be released; Li Su's lab at Academia Sinica is a likely partner for Gezaixi data.
  7. Look into Japanese traditional notation (shakuhachi honkyoku, gagaku, Noh) encoding and datasets, and minority-music (e.g. Taiwanese Indigenous polyphony) corpora. Neither was searched this round.
  8. Look for representations of heterophony and improvisation: multi-stream contour alignment, for example in jingju jinghu versus voice. Not searched.
  9. Re-check the SymbTr licence (CC BY-NC-SA) on the live GitHub LICENSE file before relying on it.

docs.title: Looked for, not found
docs.text:
• No authoritative list of synths or players implementing MIDI 2.0 per-note pitch attributes.
  • No cents-valued pitch attribute in MEI; only quarter-tone accid.ges values were found.
  • No public gongche OMR dataset; the main system was evaluated on 39 images.
  • No standard public jianpu OMR benchmark.
  • No pitch-contour or score-level MIR study of Gezaixi singing; the only item is a lyrics and audio segmentation LBD.
  • No Carnatic generative model under the name GaMaDHaNi; it covers Hindustani only.
  • MPE, improvisation and heterophony representations, and Japanese and minority musics were not reached within budget.

docs.title: D4: Generative and algorithmic stimuli in music cognition (round 1, researcher 1)
docs.text: Scope: Q1 to Q5 of D4. Budget used: 14 tool calls. Full-text read: Harrison, Collins & Müllensiefen 2017 (MDT; first 100k chars via Europe PMC XML). Abstract pages read: Lerch et al. survey, Masclef & Keller. All other claims rest on search-result snippets only and are rated lower to match.

docs.title: Q1: How existing ability tests build their stimuli
docs.text:
• The Melodic Discrimination Test (MDT) uses automatic item generation (AIG). Base melodies come from a Markov-chain model (Racchman-Jun2015) trained on Irish folk melodies in triple time from the Essen collection. No more than 2 consecutive notes may come from the same source melody. In a 20-person pilot, generated melodies did not differ from the real source extracts in rated stylistic success (p = 0.48). This is rule-based, symbolic generation, not deep learning. | Applying modern psychometric techniques to melodic discrimination testing: IRT, CAT and AIG | https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5472621 (read via Europe PMC full-text XML) | Scientific Reports (Nature) | 2017-06 | accessed 2026-11-19 | high | method | peer-reviewed (Sci Rep, 2017)
  • MDT controlled variables: the "radicals" that drive difficulty are melody length (3 to 16 notes), contour violation and tonality violation. Each altered melody changes exactly 1 note, by at most 6 semitones. These give 20 item families in v1 and 32 in v2. The "incidentals" (base melody, odd-one-out position) vary at random. Idiom and transposition are held constant. Audio is MIDI rendered with a piano timbre at 120 bpm, with 1 s gaps between melodies. | same | same | Scientific Reports | 2017-06 | accessed 2026-11-19 | high | method | peer-reviewed
  • The Computerised Adaptive Beat Alignment Test (CA-BAT; Harrison & Müllensiefen 2018) also combines IRT, CAT and AIG. It is reliable and valid in the lab but reported as poorly suited to online testing because it needs fine perceptual discrimination. | Development and Validation of the CA-BAT | https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC6097996/ | Frontiers in Psychology (per PMC; venue not verified this run) | 2018 | accessed 2026-11-19 | medium (snippet only) | method | peer-reviewed
  • The Mistuning Perception Test (MPT; Larrouy-Maestri, Harrison & Müllensiefen 2019) is adaptive and uses vocal (sung) stimuli, calibrated with explanatory item response modelling. Validation used N = 66. It ships as a psychTestR package (mpt, with psychTestRCAT). | The mistuning perception test: A new measurement instrument | https://link.springer.com/article/10.3758/s13428-019-01225-1 ; https://rdrr.io/github/pmcharrison/mpt/f/README.md | Behavior Research Methods (Springer) | 2019 | accessed 2026-11-19 | medium (snippet only) | method | peer-reviewed (BRM, 2019)
  • PROMS (Law & Zentner 2012) has 9 same/different subtests: melody, pitch, timbre, tuning, rhythm, embedded rhythm, metric accent, tempo, loudness. Short-, Mini- and Micro-PROMS versions exist (the Micro version takes 10 min or less). The official guide calls the stimuli "culture-fair". How the stimuli were built was not retrieved. | Assessing Musical Abilities Objectively: Construction and Validation of PROMS ; PROMS User Guide | https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC3532219/ ; https://musemap.org/resources/proms | PLoS One / musemap.org | 2012 / guide 2025-10 | accessed 2026-11-19 | medium (snippet only) | method | peer-reviewed (PLoS One, 2012)
  • I found no evidence that any established music-ability test uses generative-AI (deep-model) items. The AIG that does exist (MDT, CA-BAT) is rule-based or Markov-chain. | (absence across searches above) | - | - | - | accessed 2026-11-19 | medium | availability

docs.title: Q2: Deep generative models as experimental stimuli (2022 to 2026)
docs.text:
• Most recent studies that use AI music as stimuli test attitudes and provenance bias (does a "human" vs "AI" label change responses?). They do not use deep models to manipulate controlled variables. Examples:
  • PLOS One audiovisual study, N = 88: AI music from simple and detailed prompts; it produced greater pupil dilation and was rated more exciting, while human music felt more familiar.
  • Narrative-listening study (Cognitive Research: Principles & Implications, 2026): an AI label reduced imagined narratives, even when the music was actually human-made.
  • arXiv 2512.02785: attitude toward AI was the best predictor of liking.
  • 2026 detection study, N = 120: Suno and Udio outputs against commercial tracks.

| Search snippets: PMC12194076, PMC12953833, arXiv 2512.02785, Springer CRPI supplement | https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12194076/ ; https://arxiv.org/html/2512.02785 ; https://media.springernature.com/original/springer-static/esm/art%3A10.1186%2Fs41235-026-00715-z/MediaObjects/41235_2026_715_MOESM1_ESM.docx | various | 2025-2026 | accessed 2026-11-19 | medium (snippets; journal matches for each PMC ID not verified) | method | mixed (PLOS One and CRPI peer-reviewed; 2512.02785 preprint) - Validation practices seen so far: manipulation checks (e.g., "how believable is it that this clip is AI-made", 6-point scale), familiarity ratings, and matching on context (identical video). I did not find formal validation of stimulus naturalness or variable control in any of these studies. | same | same | - | 2025-2026 | accessed 2026-11-19 | low-medium | method - Deep models used as models of expectation, not as stimulus generators: a pre-trained diffusion model's surprisal shows an inverted-U relation with liking. Its fit is competitive with IDyOM. | Deep Generative Models of Music Expectation (Masclef & Keller) | https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.03500 | arXiv | 2023-10 | accessed 2026-11-19 | medium | capability | preprint - Jahrbuch Musikpsychologie (2024) compared ChatGPT and Google Magenta melody continuations against human ones in a standardized online task, controlling rater experience and probe position. | Jahrbuch Musikpsychologie record | https://doaj.org/article/28efaa8731cf47929d0d687ff4b68984 | Jahrbuch Musikpsychologie | 2024-09 | accessed 2026-11-19 | low-medium (snippet only) | method | peer-reviewed (journal) - A UAB undergraduate thesis proposes using generative AI to produce annotated stimulus datasets. Its rationale: controlled, unfamiliar stimuli are scarce in music cognition research. This states the motivation, not evidence that the approach works. | PolVierge TFG | https://ddd.uab.cat/pub/tfg/2024/tfg_8956150/PolVierge-TFG.pdf | UAB (thesis, not peer-reviewed) | 2024 | accessed 2026-11-19 | low | method

docs.title: Q3: Critiques and cross-cultural efforts
docs.text:
• The MDT authors themselves acknowledge that it uses a single idiom (Irish folk), with conformity to cultural schemata held constant, and tests pitch only (not rhythm). | Harrison et al. 2017 | https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5472621 | Sci Rep | 2017-06 | accessed 2026-11-19 | high | method | peer-reviewed
  • Jacoby and colleagues: participants come mostly from WEIRD societies and materials are mostly Western music; they call for comparative cross-cultural methods. | Search snippet (par.nsf.gov copy) | https://par.nsf.gov/servlets/purl/10169558 | NSF PAR | n/a | accessed 2026-11-19 | medium (snippet only) | method
  • Rhythm-prior study: 39 groups in 15 countries (Jacoby et al., Nature Human Behaviour 2024). Every group preferred simple integer ratios, but which ratios differed by group (e.g., Turkey, Mali, Bulgaria, Botswana). Student and online samples looked like US listeners, so "including more countries online is not enough". | MIT News / MPI Empirical Aesthetics news; DOI 10.1038/s41562-023-01800-9 | https://www.aesthetics.mpg.de/en/research/former-departments-and-research-groups/research-group-computational-auditory-perception/news/news-rg-cap-detail/article/rhythm-diversity-different-cultures-prefer-different-beat-patterns-1.html | MPI / MIT | 2024-03 | accessed 2026-11-19 | medium (press releases; paper not read) | benchmark | peer-reviewed (NHB, 2024)
  • Validation of the Music Ear Test on a Chinese sample: the authors report no prior formal translation or cross-cultural reliability and validity testing for that population. | Validation and applicability of the music ear test on a large Chinese sample | https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC10849222/ | PLoS One (per PMC; not verified) | 2024 | accessed 2026-11-19 | medium (snippet) | method | peer-reviewed
  • A Keio University-led global network plans 6 experiments on cross-cultural perception and production of rhythm, melody and harmony. | Keio KGRI project page | https://www.keio.ac.jp/en/org/kgri/project/2020/C20-05-4/ | Keio University | 2020 project | accessed 2026-11-19 | low | availability

docs.title: Q4: Evaluating generated-music quality and controllability
docs.text:
• The ACM Computing Surveys review (Lerch, Arthur, Bryan-Kinns et al.) covers evaluation targets, methods and metrics across subjective vs objective, qualitative vs quantitative, and empirical vs computational. | Survey on the Evaluation of Generative Models in Music | https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.05104 | arXiv; listed as accepted at ACM CSUR | 2025-06 (v4 2025-09) | accessed 2026-11-19 | high (existence) | method | peer-reviewed (accepted ACM CSUR, per arXiv comment)
  • Common practice: MOS and head-to-head listening tests, and Turing-style human-vs-AI tests (critiqued for rewarding imitation over creativity). There is no standardized subjective protocol. Symbolic output must be synthesized to audio, which is itself a perceptual confound. | A Comprehensive Survey for Evaluation Methodologies of AI-Generated Music | https://arxiv.org/pdf/2308.13736 | arXiv | 2023-08 | accessed 2026-11-19 | medium (snippet) | method | preprint
  • Objective metrics correlate weakly with listening tests. One benchmark reports IS correlations of 0.25 to 0.37 with subjective scores, and FAD correlations of -0.01 to -0.16. | A Benchmarking Initiative for Audio-Domain Music Generation Using the Freesound Loop Dataset | https://arxiv.org/pdf/2108.01576 | arXiv (ISMIR 2021 per my unverified belief) | 2021-08 | accessed 2026-11-19 | medium (snippet; historical) | benchmark | preprint (venue unverified)

docs.title: Q5: Generated items combined with IRT difficulty modelling
docs.text:
• Yes, a precedent exists, and it is pre-deep-learning. The MDT uses explanatory IRT:
  • Model: a constrained 3PL with guessing = 1/3, inattention = 1 and a shared discrimination of 1.31.
  • Identical Siblings Model: items in a family share one difficulty.
  • Item difficulty regressed on the radicals gives adjusted R² = 0.869. Longer melodies are harder; contour and especially tonality violations make items easier.
  • Calibration: 1,200 items, 158 adults and 266 children.
  • Reliability: test-retest r = 0.67 at 11 items. Convergent validity: r = 0.53 with the Musical Ear Test (MET) and r = 0.44 with musical training.

This is the template for "generate items with known features, then predict difficulty". | Harrison et al. 2017 | https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5472621 | Sci Rep | 2017-06 | accessed 2026-11-19 | high | method/benchmark | peer-reviewed - The same IRT+CAT+AIG approach appears in CA-BAT and, through explanatory IRT, in the MPT. All are built on psychTestR/psychTestRCAT. | CA-BAT, MPT sources above | see above | - | 2018-2019 | accessed 2026-11-19 | medium | method | peer-reviewed - I found no study that combines deep-generative (neural) items with IRT difficulty calibration in music. | (absence) | - | - | - | accessed 2026-11-19 | medium | availability

docs.title: Leads
docs.text:
• Main gap: IRT+AIG music tests exist (MDT, CA-BAT, MPT). Deep generative stimuli exist, but only in attitude and bias studies. Nobody evidenced this run bridges the two. Next round: search for any 2024 to 2026 attempt directly (queries such as "neural item generation music test" or "LLM item generation auditory test").
  • Read the rest of the MDT paper (Europe PMC XML, offset 100000) for the discussion of limitations and AIG.
  • Other tests from the same group not yet checked: the Mistuning test's source stimuli, the Gold-MSI Beat Perception and Melody Memory subtests, the Pitch Imagery Arrow Task (PIAT), and the newer psychTestR tests (e.g., the Jack & Jill / SAA singing tests). Also check whether Gold-MSI test items are generated or hand-made.
  • PROMS calls itself "culture-free", while Jacoby et al. show culture-specific rhythm priors. This contradiction is worth chasing: has PROMS been validated outside Europe?
  • Jacoby et al.'s iterated-reproduction / "serial reproduction" paradigm is itself an algorithmic way to generate culturally grounded stimuli. Look at the Computational Auditory Perception group's PsyNet tooling.
  • Harrison's later work (e.g., Mistuning, and the Long Tone / Melody singing tests) and the Mullensiefen group's "AIG" follow-ups after 2020.
  • Read the Lerch et al. CSUR survey for its recommendations on controllability metrics (attribute-control accuracy, style classifiers).
  • Verify the PMC12194076 and PMC12953833 journal identities and methods (both are AI-stimulus studies).

docs.title: Looked for, not found
docs.text:
• Any established music-ability test (Gold-MSI, PROMS, MET, MDT, CA-BAT, MPT) whose items are made with deep generative / AI models: none found.
  • A 2022 to 2026 music-cognition study that used a deep generative model to manipulate controlled variables (e.g., tonality or complexity knobs) and validated naturalness: not found. The closest are bias studies and the diffusion-surprisal preprint.
  • Neural AIG combined with IRT calibration in music: not found.
  • PROMS stimulus-construction details (synthesis, timbres, manipulations): not retrieved.
  • Controllability-specific evaluation (e.g., attribute-accuracy or style-classification accuracy) used in psychology stimulus work: not found this round.

docs.title: D5: Practical roadmap and implementation reality (round 1, digest 1)
docs.text: Budget used: 14 tool calls. 9 sources read directly (PyPI, 3 GitHub repos, 5 arXiv pages); 3 searches were used to find more. Format: claim | source title | URL | publisher | pub_date | accessed | confidence | class | peer-review status

docs.title: Q1: Standard recipe, tokenizers, pretrained models, licences
docs.text:
• The current MidiTok release is 3.1.0 (released 2026-09-30) under the MIT licence. It supports REMI, REMI+, MIDI-Like, TSD, BEAT, Structured, CPWord (Compound Word), Octuple, MuMIDI, MMM and PerTok. Tokenizers can be pushed to and loaded from the Hugging Face Hub (push_to_hub / from_pretrained). | miditok on PyPI | https://pypi.org/project/miditok/ | PyPI | 2026-09 | accessed 2026-11-19 | high | availability/licence | n/a
  • Anticipatory Music Transformer: code is Apache-2.0. Pretrained checkpoints are hosted by Stanford CRFM on Hugging Face (e.g. stanford-crfm/music-medium-800k). The README shows accompaniment from a melody out of the box: extract the melody instrument, pass it as controls= to generate(), then combine. Training uses Levanter (JAX). The README has no fine-tuning instructions. | jthickstun/anticipation README | https://github.com/jthickstun/anticipation | GitHub (Stanford) | n.d. (live page) | accessed 2026-11-19 | high | licence/availability/method | n/a
  • Paper: anticipatory infilling models match autoregressive models on prompted generation and also support infilling and accompaniment. Listeners rated 20-second accompaniments as similar in musicality to human-composed music. Trained on Lakh MIDI. | Anticipatory Music Transformer | https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.08620 | arXiv / TMLR | 2023-06 (TMLR accepted version) | accessed 2026-11-19 | high (one source) | method/benchmark | peer-reviewed (TMLR, per arXiv comment)
  • Aria (EleutherAI): code and weights are Apache-2.0. It uses the LLaMA 3.2 1B architecture and was trained on about 60k hours of transcribed expressive solo piano (Aria-MIDI dataset on HF). Released checkpoints are aria-medium-gen (continuation) and aria-medium-embedding. Inference runs on CUDA and on MLX (Apple Silicon). The README gives no fine-tuning instructions or training hardware. Piano only, performance-style (expressive) MIDI. | EleutherAI/aria README | https://github.com/EleutherAI/aria | GitHub | n.d. (live page) | accessed 2026-11-19 | high | licence/availability | paper arXiv 2506.23869: README title says ISMIR 2025, BibTeX says preprint. Status unconfirmed.
  • NotaGen: the repo is MIT and no separate weight licence is stated. It works in ABC notation. Pretrained sizes are 110M, 244M and 516M. It was pretrained on 1.6M ABC pieces and fine-tuned on about 9K classical works with "period-composer-instrumentation" prompts. The pretrained (not fine-tuned) weights cannot do prompted generation. CLaMP-DPO is an RL step that needs no human labels. | NotaGen repo; NotaGen paper | https://github.com/ElectricAlexis/NotaGen ; https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.18008 | GitHub / arXiv | 2025-02 (v5 2025-03) | accessed 2026-11-19 | high (licence: medium, weights unstated) | licence/method/dataset-size | preprint (no venue on arXiv page)
  • MIDI-GPT (Metacreation/SFU + Steinberg) is a multitrack model of about 20M parameters (GPT-2, 6 layers, 2048-token context) trained on GigaMIDI. It supports track-level infilling, bar-level infilling, and attribute controls (instrument, style, note density, polyphony, note duration), with optional velocity and microtiming. Weights are under Open RAIL-M (use-restricted, not OSI). Its tokenization (MMM) ships in MidiTok. | MIDI-GPT | https://arxiv.org/html/2501.17011v2 | arXiv | 2025-02 | accessed 2026-11-19 | high | method/licence | preprint
  • Synthesis (inference, not a single-source fact): the 2025–26 practical recipe is a MidiTok tokenizer (REMI-family or MMM for multitrack) plus a decoder-only transformer, or an ABC text model (NotaGen, ChatMusician-style LLMs). Pretrained open checkpoints now exist for each of the user's goals: AMT for accompaniment given a melody, Aria for expressive piano, NotaGen for composer/period-conditioned scores, MIDI-GPT for multitrack infilling plus attribute control. This favours adopting and fine-tuning over training from scratch. | (multiple above) | — | — | — | — | medium | method

docs.title: Q2: Compute reality
docs.text:
• MIDI-GPT (about 20M params) trains in "2-3 days using 4 V100 GPUs", roughly 200–300 V100-hours. This is the scale of from-scratch training for a small multitrack model. | MIDI-GPT | https://arxiv.org/html/2501.17011v2 | arXiv | 2025-02 | accessed 2026-11-19 | high (one source) | compute | preprint
  • NotaGen-large needs at least 24GB of GPU memory for training/fine-tuning and inference. Smaller variants (110M/244M) can be swapped in via finetune/config.py. Local NotaGen-X inference needs about 8GB. A 24GB consumer card (RTX 3090/4090) covers fine-tuning NotaGen-large; 8–16GB cards are limited to the smaller variants. | NotaGen repo | https://github.com/ElectricAlexis/NotaGen | GitHub | n.d. | accessed 2026-11-19 | high | compute | n/a
  • Aria runs on Apple Silicon via MLX for inference, which gives a no-cloud option for experiments on a Mac. | EleutherAI/aria | https://github.com/EleutherAI/aria | GitHub | n.d. | accessed 2026-11-19 | high | compute/availability | n/a

docs.title: Q3: General LLMs on ABC/symbolic music
docs.text:
• ABC-Eval (10 sub-tasks, 1,086 items) tested 7 LLMs. Overall averages: GPT-5 55.0%, GPT-5-mini 53.5%, DeepSeek-reasoner 52.0%, Gemini-2.5-pro 51.3%, GPT-5-nano 49.0%, Gemini-flash 44.1%, DeepSeek-chat 40.2%. These are averages over mixed metrics. "All foundation models failed" segment-level tasks (next-bar prediction, bar ordering, error detection). Emotion, composer and genre recognition were near chance (25%). Performance on bar counting was unstable across prompts. | ABC-Eval: Benchmarking LLMs on symbolic music | https://arxiv.org/html/2509.23350v1 | arXiv | 2025-09 | accessed 2026-11-19 | high (one source; second-source corroboration pending) | benchmark | preprint. Over 6 months old, so historical.
  • Fine-tuning LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct on ABC (SFT, DPO) improves music understanding, with SFT best. On generation, perplexity favoured SFT and ChatMusician while DPO got worse. FMD showed no clear trend. Domain gains came at the cost of general ability (MMLU), with ChatMusician losing most. The authors list compute and context-length limits as a block on multi-part scores. | How Far Can Pretrained LLMs Go in Symbolic Music? | https://arxiv.org/html/2601.22764v1 | arXiv | 2026-01 | accessed 2026-11-19 | medium | benchmark/method | preprint
  • MSU-Bench (1,800 QA items, more than 15 models) reports a gap between ABC-text and PDF-score understanding. Known only from the search snippet; the paper was not read. | MSU-Bench | https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.20697v2 | arXiv | 2025-11 (rev 2026-01) | accessed 2026-11-19 | low | benchmark | preprint
  • Synthesis: the evidence shows general LLMs are weak at bar-level structural reasoning in ABC. They are usable for metadata and syntax-level work and natural-language front-ends, not as the core generator. | (above) | — | — | — | — | medium | capability

docs.title: Q4: Conditioning techniques
docs.text:
• Anticipation (interleaving control events such as a melody ahead of the generated stream) gives melody-to-accompaniment with an existing checkpoint, through a documented API. It is the lowest-effort route to goal (a). | AMT README + paper | https://github.com/jthickstun/anticipation | GitHub/TMLR | — | accessed 2026-11-19 | high | method
  • Prompt or control-token conditioning (period-composer-instrumentation) is how NotaGen does style/composer control. It requires fine-tuned weights; the pretrained weights do not respond. | NotaGen repo | https://github.com/ElectricAlexis/NotaGen | GitHub | — | accessed 2026-11-19 | high | method
  • Attribute control tokens (density, polyphony, duration, instrument, style) plus track/bar infilling are implemented in MIDI-GPT, with tokenization in MidiTok. The authors report attribute control as effective for steering. | MIDI-GPT | https://arxiv.org/html/2501.17011v2 | arXiv | 2025-02 | accessed 2026-11-19 | medium | method | preprint
  • Pitfall: naively fine-tuning a pretrained model on new fine-grained (bar-level) controls often fails to make it follow them. MuseBarControl adds a control-pretraining stage plus a counterfactual loss: chord accuracy 78.3% vs 65.3% for plain fine-tuning (built on MuseCoco). Known from the search snippet only. | MuseBarControl | https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.04331 | arXiv | 2024-07 | accessed 2026-11-19 | low-medium | method/benchmark | preprint (status not checked)
  • Inference-time activation steering for attribute control without retraining has been proposed for the Multitrack Music Transformer. Not verified. | Latent Space Disentanglement via Activation Steering | https://arxiv.org/pdf/2605.31295 | arXiv | 2026-05 | accessed 2026-11-19 | low | method | preprint

docs.title: Q5: Pitfalls beyond monophony
docs.text:
• Copying in symbolic transformers stems from local overfitting to short recurring motifs: frequent motifs get lower perplexity and reappear in outputs. Tested mitigations are label smoothing, transposition augmentation and top-k sampling. | Why Do Music Models Plagiarize? A Motif-Centric Perspective | https://neurips.cc/virtual/2025/123788 | NeurIPS 2025 (workshop per snippet) | 2025 | accessed 2026-11-19 | medium (snippet only) | method/pitfall | workshop paper
  • Melody-based plagiarism measures assume monophony and break on polyphony. SSIMuse adapts SSIM to piano rolls for training-free replication detection in polyphonic music. | SSIMuse | https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.13658 | arXiv | 2025-09 | accessed 2026-11-19 | medium (snippet) | pitfall/eval | preprint
  • MIDI-GPT reports that duplication of training excerpts falls as generated length grows, and that infills of 4 or more bars are reliably original (Jaccard). Deployed products check for and regenerate infills identical to the source. | MIDI-GPT | https://arxiv.org/html/2501.17011v2 | arXiv | 2025-02 | accessed 2026-11-19 | high (one source) | pitfall/eval | preprint
  • Full-song multitrack work reports memorisation ratios as high as 55% on some checkpoints and none on others. A piano-transformer study found overfitting checkpoints sound more coherent while validation loss worsens, a warning that loss and "sounds good" can both hide memorisation. Both known from search snippets only. | PhraseVAE/PhraseLDM; arXiv 2511.07268 | https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.11348 ; https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.07268v2 | arXiv | 2025-12; 2025-11 | accessed 2026-11-19 | low-medium | pitfall | preprints
  • Evaluation difficulty: FMD showed no clear trends and "may not correlate well with human judgments" (2601.22764). Human listening tests remain the reference (AMT, NotaGen A/B tests). | (above) | — | — | — | — | medium | eval

docs.title: Leads
docs.text:
• Contradiction: Aria's README title says ISMIR 2025 but its BibTeX says arXiv preprint. Check the ISMIR 2025 proceedings.
  • NotaGen weights licence: the repo is MIT but the HF model cards may differ. Check HF cards. Also check its venue (possibly IJCAI 2025, unverified).
  • AMT checkpoint sizes (small/medium/large) and parameter counts, and whether HF fine-tuning works on a 24GB GPU (Levanter is JAX/TPU-oriented). Check the HF model cards and the train/ directory.
  • ChatMusician and MuPT licences and sizes (not checked this round).
  • Classifier-free guidance applied to symbolic transformers: no source found this round.
  • MidiTok "attribute controls" feature (in 3.x?) as a ready-made control-token implementation. Check MidiTok docs.
  • Free-tier cloud (Colab/Kaggle T4 16GB) feasibility for LoRA fine-tuning of NotaGen-small/medium or AMT-small.
  • Second source for the ABC-Eval conclusions (MSU-Bench full paper; ACL 2026 paper aclanthology 2026.acl-long.493).
  • Activation steering (2605.31295) is a no-retraining control option worth verifying for a low-compute user.

docs.title: Looked for, not found
docs.text:
• Reported GPU-hours for training AMT, Aria or NotaGen: not on their READMEs or arXiv abstracts. Only MIDI-GPT reported compute (4×V100, 2–3 days).
  • Official fine-tuning instructions in the AMT and Aria repos: none (only a NotaGen finetune/ config).
  • A licence statement for NotaGen weights separate from the MIT code licence.
  • Any 2026 evaluation of general LLMs generating (rather than understanding) multi-voice ABC/MusicXML with natural-language control and human ratings.
  • Direct evidence on classifier-free guidance for symbolic music control.

docs.title: Gaps R2-1: Japanese / Indigenous archives, non-Western generators, fine-tuning reports, singing synthesis
docs.text: Researcher digest, round 2. Accessed 2026-11-19. Budget: 15 tool calls. Primary pages read: the FT-GAN project page, the FT-GAN repo README, its data README and ApplyForm.txt, the GitHub API licence fields for 7 repos, and the Academia Sinica project page. Everything else rests on search-engine summaries of primary pages, and its confidence is lowered to match. Search summaries are aggregators, so I give their underlying URLs.

docs.title: Q5 Singing voice synthesis (score-to-singing)
docs.text:
• FT-GAN does Chinese opera singing synthesis, with Gezi / Taiwanese opera (​歌仔​戲​) as the main case and Peking opera also tested. Code is public at github.com/zhengmidon/Gezi-Opera-Synthesis. The model is built on the DiffSinger codebase and uses DiffSinger's pretrained HiFiGAN vocoder and pitch extractor. | FT-GAN: Fine-Grained Tune Modeling for Chinese Opera Synthesis (project page + repo README) | https://zhengmidon.github.io/FTGAN.github.io/ ; https://github.com/zhengmidon/Gezi-Opera-Synthesis | Zheng, Bai, Shi, Zhou, Yan (Xiamen Univ.) | 2024-02 | accessed 2026-11-19 | high | availability | peer-reviewed (AAAI 2024, pp. 19697–19705, doi:10.1609/AAAI.V38I17.29943)
  • The FT-GAN code repo has no licence file: the GitHub API returns license: None, and the last push was 2024-02-29 (9 stars). Without a licence, all rights are reserved by default, so the code cannot be reused as-is. | GitHub API, repos/zhengmidon/Gezi-Opera-Synthesis | https://api.github.com/repos/zhengmidon/Gezi-Opera-Synthesis | GitHub | live | accessed 2026-11-19 | high (single authoritative source, live) | licence
  • The GOAT Gezi opera dataset is released on application only. You email a signed form to the authors, and the form says the dataset licence is "CC by-nc-sa 4.0 (NonCommercial!)". You must also indemnify the authors against claims arising from "copies of copyrighted audio files". The project page does not state the dataset's size in hours. | data/README.md + data/ApplyForm.txt | https://github.com/zhengmidon/Gezi-Opera-Synthesis/tree/master/data | FT-GAN authors | 2024-02 | accessed 2026-11-19 | high | licence
  • The FT-GAN paper claims it beats strong SVS baselines on naturalness and expressiveness for Gezi opera. This is the authors' own evaluation and no independent replication was found. | AAAI paper (via search summary) | https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/29943 | AAAI | 2024 | accessed 2026-11-19 | low-medium (self-reported, abstract-level only) | benchmark
  • openvpi/DiffSinger (the community successor to DiffSinger) is Apache-2.0, actively maintained (pushed 2026-11-19, about 3.2k stars), and describes itself as an SVS system with "controllability and flexibility". | GitHub API | https://api.github.com/repos/openvpi/DiffSinger | GitHub | live | accessed 2026-11-19 | high | licence/availability
  • The original MoonInTheRiver/DiffSinger repo is MIT-licensed (AAAI 2022 official code, pushed 2026-07). Note that the licence covers the code. The licences of the pretrained checkpoints and the singing data they were trained on, which FT-GAN depends on, were not verified. | GitHub API | https://api.github.com/repos/MoonInTheRiver/DiffSinger | GitHub | live | accessed 2026-11-19 | high (code licence) | licence
  • openvpi/SOME (Singing-Oriented MIDI Extractor) is MIT-licensed. It is relevant to transcribing singing into note sequences. | GitHub API | https://api.github.com/repos/openvpi/SOME | GitHub | live | accessed 2026-11-19 | high | licence

docs.title: Q4 Fine-tuning reports
docs.text:
• The NotaGen repo is MIT-licensed (last push 2025-04). Per search excerpts of its README, it includes a fine-tuning recipe with a small demo dataset of Schubert lieder from OpenScore Lieder, plus ABC↔MusicXML conversion. The authors' demo page reports fine-tuning on about 100 popular songs, followed by RL, to get a pop style. Compute figures for that fine-tune were not found. | GitHub API; NotaGen demo page / repo (via search summary) | https://github.com/ElectricAlexis/NotaGen ; https://electricalexis.github.io/notagen-demo | Wang et al. | 2025 | accessed 2026-11-19 | high (licence), medium (recipe, ~100 songs; README not read directly) | licence / method | paper peer-reviewed (IJCAI 2025)
  • Anticipatory Music Transformer: code and models are Apache-2.0 (repo pushed 2026-07). The repo has preprocessing and sampling code but no training code, and the authors point to the Levanter codebase for training. The Large 780M model was trained on Lakh + MetaMIDI + transcripts of FMA and 450k commercial records. That data provenance matters for commercial use. No third-party fine-tuning report was found. One HF repo (william590y/beatalignment) contains a training README but was not read. | GitHub API; HF model card; arXiv 2306.08620 (via search summary) | https://github.com/jthickstun/anticipation ; https://huggingface.co/stanford-crfm/music-large-800k | Thickstun et al. / Stanford CRFM | 2023-06 | accessed 2026-11-19 | high (licence), medium (training-data claims) | licence / method | paper: TMLR 2024 is my belief, unverified this run; the arXiv version is a preprint
  • The Aria repo (EleutherAI/aria) is Apache-2.0 (pushed 2026-05). It describes itself as the official repo for "Scaling Self-Supervised Representation Learning for Symbolic Piano Performance (ISMIR 2025)". No fine-tuning reports were found this run. | GitHub API | https://api.github.com/repos/EleutherAI/aria | GitHub | live | accessed 2026-11-19 | high | licence | peer-reviewed (ISMIR 2025), as stated by the repo

docs.title: Q3 Generators for non-Western / non-12-TET music
docs.text:
• MusicMamba generates melodies in Chinese traditional modes, trained on about 300 self-compiled pieces. An HF page hosts an implementation and checkpoints and says fine-tuning is not offered. The GitHub repo I guessed (xinyu1205/MusicMamba) returned 404, so the code location and licence are unverified. | MusicMamba (arXiv 2409.02421); HF moersxm12138/MusicMamba (via search summary) | https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.02421 ; https://huggingface.co/moersxm12138/MusicMamba | — | 2024-09 | accessed 2026-11-19 | medium-low | capability/availability | preprint
  • SongSong (arXiv 2602.24071, Feb 2026) generates ancient Chinese SongCi music and releases a dataset, OpenSongSong, of 29.9 hours. Whether the code and licence are released was not verified. | arXiv 2602.24071 (via search summary) | https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.24071 | — | 2026-02 | accessed 2026-11-19 | medium-low | dataset-size/capability | preprint
  • CPTGZ is a latent diffusion model that generates guzheng music from Chinese paintings. No code release was found. | IEEE Access (via DOAJ) | https://doaj.org/article/07f3ba106248461481073364b09feea8 | IEEE Access | 2024-01 | accessed 2026-11-19 | low | capability | peer-reviewed (IEEE Access 2024), per search summary
  • Makam: ATMMC is a deep-learning symbolic composer for Turkish makam music that takes 8 seed notes. Its own paper says there is "scarcely any work" on automatic makam composition. | Turkish J. Elec. Eng. & Comp. Sci. 29(7) (via search summary) | https://aj.tubitak.gov.tr/elektrik/issues/elk-21-29-7/elk-29-7-13-2101-44.pdf | TÜBİTAK | 2021 | accessed 2026-11-19 | low-medium | capability | peer-reviewed journal (historical, more than 6 months old)
  • Raga: GaMaDHaNi models Hindustani vocal pitch contours, which are continuous rather than 12-TET, using a transformer over discrete tokens plus diffusion. Its authors say it does not condition on tonic, raga or tala. A 2026 benchmark (arXiv 2606.05522, CC BY 4.0, per search summary) reports that even the best LLM produces stylistically faithful raga outputs only about 40% of the time. | arXiv 2408.12658; arXiv 2606.05522 (via search summary) | https://arxiv.org/html/2408.12658v2 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2606.05522v1 | — | 2024-08 / 2026-06 | accessed 2026-11-19 | low-medium | capability/benchmark | GaMaDHaNi: ISMIR 2024 is my belief, unverified; 2606.05522 is a preprint

docs.title: Q1 Japanese traditional music
docs.text:
• VocalNotes (ISMIR 2023 LBD) has pitch and note annotations by experts across 5 vocal traditions. The Japanese min'yō part is 9 recordings (3 singers × 3 songs). docs.title: Leads
docs.text:
1. Licence stack conflict for Gezi-opera SVS. The FT-GAN code has no licence, the GOAT data is NC-SA with an indemnity clause, and it depends on DiffSinger checkpoints whose own licence is unverified. Openvpi/DiffSinger (Apache-2.0) is the cleaner base, but its pretrained models and voicebanks may carry separate terms. Next: check the openvpi model and voicebank terms, and email the FT-GAN authors to ask for a code licence.
  2. AMT data provenance. The Large model was trained on "450k commercial records" transcripts, while the Apache-2.0 model licence covers only the code and weights. Assess the commercial-use risk. The small Lakh-only models may be safer.
  3. Read the NotaGen README fine-tune section directly to get GPU and hours numbers. Look for NotaGen GitHub issues about fine-tuning on folk or non-Western ABC (Chinese jianpu → ABC is a candidate pipeline).
  4. Read SongSong / OpenSongSong (2602.24071) for the code and data licence. It is the most recent Chinese-traditional generator found, at 29.9 h.
  5. Japanese: search the Japanese-language literature (e.g. "​邦​楽​ データセット", "​尺八​ ​自動​採譜​", the ​情報​処​理学​会​ SIGMUS proceedings) and NII / Geidai digital archives. English searches found nothing MIR-ready.
  6. Chinese ethnic minority archives: not searched this run because of budget. Candidates to chase: the Chinese Academy of Arts music research institute sound archive and the CCMusic database (licence check).
  7. Academia Sinica: the reuse terms must come from the museum's or the Taiwan Ethnography Video and Audio Archive's general copyright page, or from the contact address. Indigenous consent norms (CARE principles, the Indigenous Peoples Basic Law) probably apply beyond copyright.

docs.title: Red team C1: "Adopt and fine-tune existing open symbolic models"
docs.text: Run date: 2026-11-19. Budget: 15 tool calls. Sources were retrieved this run. Anything marked "unverified belief" was not evidenced.

docs.title: Verdict
docs.text:
Weakened, not overturned. I found no evidence that training a small model from scratch beats fine-tuning these four models, whether in general or for non-Western or Chinese-opera material. No study made that comparison directly, so the core "adopt, don't train" strategy stands. But several parts of the conclusion as written are overstated:

  1. "Feasible on 24GB" holds only partly. The NotaGen README says NotaGen-large needs at least 24GB to train, so a 24GB card is at the ceiling and in practice means NotaGen-small or NotaGen-medium. The Aria model card gives no fine-tuning instructions and no memory figures.
  2. The licence and provenance situation is weaker than "open" suggests. The AMT authors say Lakh MIDI's CC-BY label hides heterogeneous, mostly undocumented copyright on derivative pop transcriptions. They say outputs "should be presumed to risk infringing". The NotaGen repo does not name its 1.6M-piece pretraining sources. The Aria-MIDI dataset is CC-BY-NC-SA, although the Aria weights are Apache-2.0. Stimuli for non-commercial academic use are probably still publishable. That is an unverified belief, not legal advice. But stimulus sets cannot be called "clean", and commercial reuse is unclear.
  3. "Culturally diverse" is the weakest part. Western-default behaviour is documented, but for audio models (MusicGen, Mustango) and as an argument about the MIDI format. Symbolic studies make the same case from data and format analysis rather than benchmarks. Machine-readable Peking-opera (jingju) scores exist, but no prior symbolic jingju generation model turned up. The related jingju data is CC-BY-NC. A small pretrained-then-fine-tuned Music Transformer memorised a 32-piece fine-tuning set. That makes overfitting and copying a concrete risk at jingju-corpus scale. It also means the evaluation layer has to include memorisation checks such as LCS or n-gram overlap.
  4. Text2midi has thin evaluation. Its listening test used 5 generated files, and later work had to realign test splits to compare against it.

The strongest good-faith case for a small custom model is this. For a tradition whose pitch inflection and ornamentation fit 12-TET MIDI or ABC tokens poorly, a custom tokenizer may matter more than pretrained weights. It is also the only way to control training-data provenance fully. A small model trained on a few hundred scores has little capacity to memorise beyond what it is given, and both the data and its licence are fully known. This argument is plausible but unverified: no paper retrieved this run shows it winning.

docs.title: Red-team C2: two-layer symbolic + contour hybrid vs end-to-end audio
docs.text:
Conclusion under attack: "For a controllable music generator meant to cover culturally diverse traditions, the best architecture is a two-layer hybrid. A discrete symbolic note/score layer carries control, and a continuous pitch-contour/performance layer rendered to audio carries expressive and non-12-TET detail. This beats generating audio end-to-end."

Budget used: 15 tool calls (1 ToolSearch, 7 WebSearch, 7 WebFetch). Run date: 2026-11-19. Most fetches read only abstract pages, so full-paper details are unverified.

docs.title: Verdict
docs.text:
Weakened, not overturned. I found no head-to-head study showing end-to-end audio beats a symbolic-plus-contour hybrid on control or quality, for any tradition. The strongest 2026 evidence partly supports the conclusion. In the YuE2 ablation, experts preferred the output when the model first wrote an explicit, readable score (49.3% vs 34.6%). But three findings undercut parts of the claim.

  1. Separate stages lost to a joint model. In YuE2, experts preferred one jointly trained model that does both the score and the audio over a separate LM plus diffusion-Transformer cascade. This favors "score as an internal planning step in one model" over "two separately built layers."
  2. Audio-only control is now strong. Adapters on audio models now give large control gains without a symbolic layer, mostly preserving quality. DiffSynth-Music raised Beat-F1 from 0.30 to 0.85 and Pitch-50 from 0.04 to 0.47. Its controls are beats, vocals, accompaniment and prosody, not melody, chords or key. An unmodified streaming audio model (Lyria RealTime), steered only by prompts, reportedly produced more off-grid quartertone maqam content.
  3. A discrete note layer is the wrong control point for some traditions. The Hindustani work GaMaDHaNi drops note symbols on purpose. It models a fine pitch contour (10-cent bins) directly, saying prescriptive notation "fails to faithfully capture the fine melodic intricacies connecting these notes." Ethnomusicology has argued since the 1970s that staff-like categories impose European structure. The JRMA article cited below adds that even flexible notations "put in place certain categorical premisses."

So the defensible version is narrower. An explicit, editable score/plan representation helps control. For contour-centric traditions, the control layer may need to be the contour itself, or a culture-specific symbolic vocabulary (as in PerFormer for Persian music), not Western-style notes. Whether the layers should be separately trained stages or one jointly trained model remains open, and 2026 evidence (YuE2) leans joint.

PEFT on MusicGen and Mustango for Hindustani and makam is "promising but non-trivial" (+8% and +4% Elo). End-to-end audio adaptation works only modestly. This shows neither architecture is proven for these traditions.

docs.text:

  • No quantified cascade-error study between a symbolic or semantic stage and audio rendering. Open-Qwen-Music (arXiv 2609.31652, 2026-09) only says its release enables this analysis. Its abstract reports no numbers.
  • No end-to-end audio model with explicit, evaluated key or tempo control in 2025–2026 results. Melody and chord control exists (JASCO, MuseControlLite, MusiConGen). DiffSynth-Music covers beat and prosody, not chords or key.
  • No published failure case or post-mortem of a two-stage symbolic-to-render system for non-Western singing, such as Taiwanese opera, Peking opera, Carnatic or makam vocals.
  • No MOS or naturalness benchmark for MIDI- or score-driven Chinese-opera or Taiwanese-opera synthesis vs end-to-end audio.
  • No Taiwanese opera (gezaixi) generation work of either type turned up, apart from the Gezi Opera FT-GAN mention (AAAI), which I did not verify in detail.
  • No computational-ethnomusicology source arguing specifically that note skeleton plus continuous contour (as opposed to staff notation alone) misrepresents a tradition. The critiques found target staff notation and discrete categories in general.

docs.title: Red team: claim C3, "neural generation + IRT for music-ability testing is an open gap"
docs.text: Skeptic pass, 2026-11-19. Budget: 15 tool calls (14 used). Web only; no local files read.

docs.title: Verdict
docs.text:
Survives, with one wording fix. I searched 12 times and fetched one page. None of it turned up a paper, preprint or thesis that uses a neural generator (transformer, VAE, diffusion or LLM) to make music-ability test items and then calibrates them with IRT or adaptive testing. The factual premise checks out against the primary source. Harrison, Collins & Müllensiefen (2017) generated their melodic discrimination base melodies with a Markov-chain model trained on Irish folk tunes from the Essen collection. Item difficulty was explained by a few controlled "radicals": length, plus contour and tonality violations (Study 1 regression, adjusted R² = 0.869). The same AIG + IRT + CAT approach was reused for CA-BAT (2018) and aPIAT (2020–21), and I found no 2024–2026 successor that uses neural generation.

The nearest work falls short of the claim in specific ways: - An ICMPC 2023 study used an EC2-VAE to make interpolated melodies for similarity ratings. These are perception stimuli, not calibrated test items, and there is no IRT. - A 2025 UAB bachelor's thesis aimed to build a set of AI-generated music stimuli for cognition research. Its own diffusion model failed, so it fell back on Suno, and it has no difficulty calibration. - A JHU paper (ICASSP 2020) synthesised surprisal-maximising melodies with the D-REX model. That is a statistical model, not a neural one, and the paper measures engagement, not ability.

Wording fix. "No published work" is a claim that something does not exist, and a 15-call web search cannot prove that. Phrase it as "no such work found in a targeted search of 2017–2026 literature."

Strongest good-faith counter-argument (my own reasoning, not taken from a retrieved source). The gap may be open because filling it is not worth much, not because nobody thought of it: 1. The Markov-chain approach already explains about 87% of difficulty variance. That leaves little room for a neural generator to improve calibration. 2. Explanatory IRT and AIG get their construct validity from interpretable, manipulable radicals (complexity, similarity). A black-box neural generator weakens that validity unless its outputs are mapped back onto those features. 3. Neural models trained on large corpora may reproduce familiar tunes or idioms. That brings in familiarity and enculturation confounds, the problem the UAB thesis was trying to avoid.

So the gap is real, but the case for filling it has to show what neural generation adds, such as stylistic range, ecological validity or new constructs. It cannot just say "nobody has done it."

  • Published critiques of AI-generated test items on validity grounds; none found, so the counter-argument above is my own reasoning

docs.title: 技術​查證​：​原型​的​三個​模型​能​不能​用
docs.text: ​這份​研究​服務​的​決定​： docs/prototype-plan-melody-to-performance/ ​的​〈​要​比​較​的​選項​〉​與​〈​平台​與​技術​〉​要​不要​改​。

docs.title: 執行​摘要
docs.text:
​建議​：​表情​演奏​的​兩個候​選換成​ SyMuPe/PianoFlow ​對​ Pianist Transformer，​拿掉​ Aria。​真正​的​風險​不​在​演奏​端​，​而​在​ AMT ​生​伴奏​這​一段​。

  1. Aria ​只能​續寫​，​不能​照譜​演奏​ [1][2][3]。​它​的​ README、​模型​卡​和​ issue ​都​沒​有​「​樂譜​→​演奏​」​的​模式​。​有​一個​用​ Aria ​微調​的​研究​版​ MAJEPPA ​能​做到​ [4][5]，​但​它​以​ CUDA ​為主​，​也​還不確​定會​不會​改動​音符​。
  2. ​兩個​演奏​模型​都​能​在​ Mac ​的​ CPU ​上​跑​，​也​都​直接​吃樂譜​ MIDI。
  3. SyMuPe/PianoFlow：​約​ 2,400 ​萬​參數​，​沒有​只能​用​ CUDA ​的​套件​，​裝置​可以​自己​指定​ [10][12]。
  4. Pianist Transformer（ICML 2026）：1.35 ​億參數​，README ​明寫​一般​ CPU ​就夠​，​附​ macOS ​安裝步​驟​，​權重​是​ Apache-2.0 [6][7]。
  5. ​但​ SyMuPe ​開源版​沒有​「​情緒​文字​引導​」，​原型​計畫列​的​這個​優點​要​拿掉​ [10][11]。
  6. AMT ​能​跑​，​但​有​三個​坑​：
  7. ​沒有​前​ 5 ​秒​的​伴奏​當開頭​，​生出​來​的​伴奏​品質​會​掉​；​這是​使用者​回報​，​作者​沒有​回應​ [18]。
  8. ​不能​指定​只用​鋼琴​伴奏​ [19]。
  9. ​舊版​相依​套件​在​ Python 3.12 ​上裝​不​起來​ [16]；​生成​很​慢​，​主​分支​沒有​ KV ​快取​ [17]。

​最大​的​限制​： ​沒​有人​回報過​這三個​模型​在​ Apple MPS ​上​的​成敗​，​只能​確定​ CPU ​可行​。​速度​要​實際​跑​過才​知道​。

docs.title: 一​、​表情​演奏​：Aria ​與​替代​方案
docs.text:
Aria ​不合​用​。 ​官方​只​提供​續寫​、MIDI ​嵌入​向量​和​即​時續​寫​的​展示​ [1][2]。​論文​評估​的​也​是​續​寫​和​分類​，​不是​演奏​渲染​（​只讀​了​搜尋​摘要​，​中​信心​）[3]。​在​ issue ​裡搜尋​ render、humanize、performance，​都​沒​有​結果​ [1]。​把​樂譜當​提示​詞​丟給​ Aria，​它​只會​往下​接著​寫​。

MAJEPPA ​是​ Aria ​的​ LoRA ​微調​版​（ISMIR 2026），​可以​輸入​樂譜​ MIDI、​輸出​演奏​ MIDI [4][5]。​不過​範例​寫​死​ device="cuda"，​也​沒​說​會​不會​保留​原本​的​音符​、​有​沒​有​輸出​踏板​（​中​信心​）。

Pianist Transformer ​最​適合​在​ Mac ​上​跑​ [6][7]： - ​輸入​是​樂譜​ MIDI，​不用​轉​ MusicXML。 - README ​寫明​「​一般​ CPU ​就夠​，​有​ GPU ​會​比​較​快​」，​附​ macOS ​安裝步​驟​（Python 3.11、PyTorch 2.7.1）。 - ​輸出​可​編輯​的​ MIDI，​包含​力度​、​運音​和​踏板​；​速度​表情​用​「​動態​速度​曲線​」​表示​。 - ​有​指令​列​，​也​有​圖形​介面​。​程式​碼​和​權重​都​是​ Apache-2.0。 - ​沒有明​講會​保留​每一個​原本​的​音符​。​用​速度​曲線​表示​速度​表情​，​暗示​音符​本身​不動​，​但​這是​推論​（​中​信心​）。

​其他​候選​比​較​不​適合​： - VirtuosoNet ​一定​要​ MusicXML，​權重​在​ HF，​授權​沒標​ [8]。 - ScorePerformer ​是非​商用​授權​，​沒有​明確​可下載​的​權重​ [9]。 - DExter ​沒有​預訓練​權重​ [14]。

docs.title: 二​、SyMuPe/PianoFlow ​在​ Mac ​上
docs.text:
• ​能​在​ CPU ​上​跑​。 ​相依​套件​裡沒有​ flash-attn、triton ​這類​只能​用​ CUDA ​的​東西​，​原始​碼​也​沒​有​寫​死​ .cuda()，​裝置​是​傳進​去​的​參數​ [10]。MPS ​應該​也​可以​，​但​沒​有人​回報過​（​中​信心​）。
  • ​輸入​是​量化​過的​樂譜​ MIDI（perform_score("score.mid")），​不​需要​對齊​好​的​演奏​資料​。​程式​預設​把​多​軌合​併​成一軌​ [10]。
  • ​很小​，​速度​夠用​。 ​約​ 2,400 ​萬​參數​；​作者​說​在​ CPU ​上​「​接近​即時​」，​但​沒​有​說​是​哪顆​ CPU（​中​信心​）[12]。
  • ​沒​有情​緒​文字​引導​。 ​論文裡​有​，​但​開源​的​ v1.1.0 ​和​ PianoFlow-base ​模型​卡​都​沒​有​提供​ [10][11][12]。
  • ​安裝要​手動​補​ numba（issue #9，​仍未修​）[13]。​權重​是​ CC BY-NC-SA，​研究​用​沒​問題​ [11]。​專案​很​新​、​維護者​少​，​最​後​一次​提交​是​ 2026-04-30 [10]。

docs.title: 三​、AMT ​在​ Mac ​上生​伴奏
docs.text:
• ​能​在​ CPU ​上​跑​。 ​核心​的​取樣​程式​不​綁定​裝置​，​只有​幾支​評估​用​的​輔助​腳本​寫​死​ .cuda()，​直接​呼叫​ generate() ​就​能​避開​ [15]。​中型​模型​約​ 3.6 ​億參數​，fp32 ​大約​ 1.4GB，18GB ​記憶體​綽綽有​餘​ [20]。
  • ​環境​要​用​舊版​ Python。 transformers==4.29.2 ​在​ Python 3.12 ​上裝​不​起來​，​有人​改用​ 3.9 ​解決​ [16]。
  • ​很​慢​。 ​主​分支​沒有​ KV ​快取​，​每加​一個​ token ​都​要​重算​整段​上下文​；​作者​另​一個​有​快取​的​分支​還沒合​併​ [17]。​查不到​ CPU ​或​ MPS ​的​速度​數字​。
  • ​給​旋律​生​伴奏​是​官方​支援​的​用法​，​但​有​前提​ [14]：
  • ​旋律​要​放在​獨立​的​樂器​（MIDI program）​上​，​才能​抽出​來當​條件​。
  • ​官方​範例​都​附​了​前​ 5 ​秒​的​真實​伴奏​當開頭​。​有​使用者​回報​，​沒有​這段​開頭​，「​幾乎​生不出​好​的​伴奏​」[18]（​單​一回​報​，​已親​自核​對​）。
  • ​不能​指定​只用​鋼琴​伴奏​ [19]。​模型​會​自己​挑樂器​；​作者​給的​遮罩​作法​會卡​在​重​複​音​和​零長​度​音符​上​。​要​接到​鋼琴​演奏​模型​，​就​得​事​後​把​所有​伴奏​軌​改成​鋼琴​。
  • ​上下文​是​ 1,024 ​個​ token，​長​曲子​用​滑動視​窗​生成​，​整首​的​連貫性​有限​ [14]。

docs.title: 跨​面向​洞察
docs.text:
• ​風險​從​演奏​端移​到​了​伴奏​端​。 ​原本​最​擔心​的​是​ Aria ​和​ SyMuPe ​跑​不​跑​得動​，​結果​演奏​端有​兩個​能​在​ CPU ​上​跑​、​直接​吃​ MIDI ​的​選項​。​反而​是​ AMT ​有三個​問題​疊​在​一起​：​需要​伴奏​開頭​、​不能​指定​鋼琴​、​速度慢​。​原型​計畫​的​放棄​條件​之一​是​「​沒有​一段​伴奏​和​旋律​搭得​起來​」，​最​可能​觸發​它​的​就是​這​一段​。
  • ​兩​端的​格式​要​對​上​。 AMT ​輸出​多種​樂器​，​兩個​演奏​模型​都​預期​單軌​鋼琴​。​中間​要​有​一步​把​所有​軌​改成​鋼琴​、​合​併​成一軌​。

docs.title: 建議
docs.text:
1. 〈​要​比​較​的​選項​〉​改成​ SyMuPe/PianoFlow ​對​ Pianist Transformer，Aria ​拿掉​。 MAJEPPA ​列為​備案​，​只​在​ Colab ​上試​。​信心​：​高​。CPU ​可行​和​輸入​格式​都​有​第一手​來源​。​音符​會不會​被​改動要​實測​。​對應​原型​計畫​〈​要​比​較​的​選項​〉。
  2. SyMuPe ​的​優點​拿掉​「​情緒​文字​引導​」。 ​信心​：​中​高​（​程式​碼​搜尋加​模型​卡​）。​對應​〈​平台​與​技術​〉​和​〈​要​比​較​的​選項​〉。
  3. AMT ​用​獨立​的​ Python 3.10 ​虛擬​環境​，​直接​呼叫​ generate()，​不用​官方​的​輔助​腳本​。​先跑​ CPU，​再試​ MPS。​信心​：​高​。​對應​〈​平台​與​技術​〉。
  4. ​把​「​沒有​伴奏​開頭​」​當成​這​次要​測的​事​。 ​每​段​旋律​試兩種​開頭​：​完全​沒有​，​以及​幾小節​簡單​的​柱式​和弦​。​生成​後​把​所有​伴奏​軌​改成​鋼琴​。​信心​：​中​（​品質​問題​只有​單​一回​報​）。​對應​〈​建置​〉。
  5. ​建置​的​第一步​先​做​煙霧​測試​：​三個​模型​各​在​ CPU ​上​跑​一小​段​，​記下​速度​，​再試​ device="mps"。​信心​：​高​。​對應​〈​建置​〉。

docs.title: 待解​問題
docs.text:
• ​三個​模型​在​ MPS ​上​的​表現​：​沒有​任何​回報​，​要​實機​測試​。
  • Pianist Transformer ​和​ PianoFlow ​會不會​改動​音符​：​要讀​原始​碼​，​或​比​較​輸入​和​輸出​的​音高​序列​。
  • AMT ​沒有​伴奏​開頭​時​的​品質​：​只有​一則​使用者​回報​，​要​實際​聽​。
  • AMT 2026 ​年​的​新​ PR（Span Anticipation、Symusic Conversion）​會不會​帶來​能​指定​樂器​的​新​模型​：​還沒合​併​到​主​分支​，​要​繼續​觀察​ [14]。
  • ​沒有查​的​部分​：Magenta ​之類​的​「MIDI ​人性化​」​工具​，​因為​助理​的​查詢​額度​用​完​了​。
